title: 彼得兔的故事
author: Beatrix Potter 比阿特麗克斯·波特
description: 《The Tales of Beatrix Potter》(1902–1909):彼得兔、班傑明兔、松鼠納特金等八個經典動物小故事,語言簡單、情節有趣,最適合初學者閱讀。

chapters.title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit 彼得兔的故事

passages.original: CH Once upon a time there were four little Rabbits, and their names were--
passages.vernacular: 從前有四隻小兔子,佢哋嘅名字係——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有四隻小兔子,他們的名字是——

passages.original: Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
passages.vernacular: 福洛西、莫洛西、棉尾巴,仲有彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福洛西、莫洛西、棉尾巴,還有彼得。

passages.original: They lived with their Mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋同媽媽住喺一個沙坡裡,就喺一棵好大嘅冷杉樹嘅樹根下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們和媽媽住在一個沙坡裡,就在一棵很大的冷杉樹的樹根下面。

passages.original: 'Now my dears,' said old Mrs. Rabbit one morning, 'you may go into the fields or down the lane, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden: your Father had an accident there; he was put in a pie by Mrs. McGregor.'
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,我嘅細路哋,」老兔太太有一天早晨講,「你哋可以去田野裡,或者沿住小路走,但係唔好去麥克格雷格先生嘅園子:你哋嘅爸爸喺嗰度出咗意外;佢被麥克格雷格太太做成咗餡餅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,我的孩子們,」老兔太太有一天早晨說,「你們可以去田野裡,或者沿著小路走,但是別去麥克格雷格先生的園子:你們的爸爸在那裡出了意外;他被麥克格雷格太太做成了餡餅。」

passages.original: 'Now run along, and don't get into mischief.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,去玩吧,別惹麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,去玩吧,別惹麻煩。

passages.original: I am going out.'
passages.vernacular: 我要出門喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要出門了。」

passages.original: Then old Mrs. Rabbit took a basket and her umbrella, and went through the wood to the baker's.
passages.vernacular: 然後老兔太太攞起一個籃子同佢嘅雨傘,穿過樹林去麵包店。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後老兔太太拿起一個籃子和她的雨傘,穿過樹林去麵包店。

passages.original: She bought a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns.
passages.vernacular: 佢買咗一條黑麵包同五個葡萄乾小圓麵包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她買了一條黑麵包和五個葡萄乾小圓麵包。

passages.original: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cottontail, who were good little bunnies, went down the lane to gather blackberries:
passages.vernacular: 福洛西、莫洛西同棉尾巴係乖巧嘅小兔子,佢哋沿住小路去採黑莓喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福洛西、莫洛西和棉尾巴是乖巧的小兔子,他們沿著小路去採黑莓了:

passages.original: But Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden, and squeezed under the gate!
passages.vernacular: 不過好淘氣嘅彼得,一直跑到麥克格雷格先生嘅園子,從大門底下擠咗進去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是非常淘氣的彼得,一直跑到麥克格雷格先生的園子,從大門底下擠了進去!

passages.original: First he ate some lettuces and some French beans; and then he ate some radishes;
passages.vernacular: 佢先食咗些萵苣同四季豆;然後又食咗些小蘿蔔;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他先吃了些萵苣和四季豆;然後又吃了些小蘿蔔;

passages.original: And then, feeling rather sick, he went to look for some parsley.
passages.vernacular: 然後覺得有點噁心,就去找些香芹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後覺得有點噁心,就去找些香芹。

passages.original: But round the end of a cucumber frame, whom should he meet but Mr. McGregor!
passages.vernacular: 不過繞過黃瓜架嘅盡頭,佢碰見嘅唔係別人,正是麥克格雷格先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是繞過黃瓜架的盡頭,他碰見的不是別人,正是麥克格雷格先生!

passages.original: Mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages, but he jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and calling out, 'Stop thief!'
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生正跪喺地上種小捲心菜,可佢跳起嚟追趕彼得,揮住一把耙子,大喊:「抓賊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生正跪在地上種小捲心菜,可他跳起來追趕彼得,揮著一把耙子,大喊:「抓賊!」

passages.original: Peter was most dreadfully frightened; he rushed all over the garden, for he had forgotten the way back to the gate.
passages.vernacular: 彼得嚇壞喇;佢喺園子裡到處亂竄,因為佢忘咗回大門嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得嚇壞了;他在園子裡到處亂竄,因為他忘了回大門的路。

passages.original: He lost one of his shoes among the cabbages, and the other shoe amongst the potatoes.
passages.vernacular: 佢把一隻鞋丟喺捲心菜中間,另一隻鞋丟喺馬鈴薯中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把一隻鞋丟在捲心菜中間,另一隻鞋丟在馬鈴薯中間。

passages.original: After losing them, he ran on four legs and went faster, so that I think he might have got away altogether if he had not unfortunately run into a gooseberry net, and got caught by the large buttons on his jacket.
passages.vernacular: 丟咗鞋子以後,佢四腳住地跑,跑得更快喇,我想佢本來或者能完全逃脫,只可惜佢不幸撞進咗一張醋栗網,被外套上嘅大鈕扣勾住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 丟了鞋子以後,他四腳著地跑,跑得更快了,我想他本來也許能完全逃脫,只可惜他不幸撞進了一張醋栗網,被外套上的大鈕扣勾住了。

passages.original: It was a blue jacket with brass buttons, quite new.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一件藍外套,帶銅鈕扣,相當新。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一件藍外套,帶銅鈕扣,相當新。

passages.original: Peter gave himself up for lost, and shed big tears; but his sobs were overheard by some friendly sparrows, who flew to him in great excitement, and implored him to exert himself.
passages.vernacular: 彼得以為自己完喇,流下大顆嘅眼淚;不過佢嘅抽泣被幾隻友好嘅麻雀聽見喇,牠哋好激動地飛到佢身邊,懇求佢振作起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得以為自己完了,流下大顆的眼淚;可是他的抽泣被幾隻友好的麻雀聽見了,牠們非常激動地飛到他身邊,懇求他振作起來。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor came up with a sieve, which he intended to pop upon the top of Peter; but Peter wriggled out just in time, leaving his jacket behind him.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生攞住一個篩子過嚟,打算把佢扣喺彼得身上;不過彼得及時扭咗出嚟,把外套留喺咗後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生拿著一個篩子過來,打算把它扣在彼得身上;可是彼得及時扭了出來,把外套留在了後面。

passages.original: And rushed into the tool-shed, and jumped into a can.
passages.vernacular: 佢衝進工具棚,跳進一個罐子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他衝進工具棚,跳進一個罐子裡。

passages.original: It would have been a beautiful thing to hide in, if it had not had so much water in it.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係裡面有咁多水,嗰本來係個好好嘅藏身之處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是裡面有那麼多水,那本來是個很好的藏身之處。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor was quite sure that Peter was somewhere in the tool-shed, perhaps hidden underneath a flower-pot.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生好肯定彼得喺工具棚嘅某個地方,或者藏喺一個花盆下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生十分肯定彼得在工具棚的某個地方,也許藏在一個花盆下面。

passages.original: He began to turn them over carefully, looking under each.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始小心地把花盆一個個翻過嚟,每個下面都睇一睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始小心地把花盆一個個翻過來,每個下面都看一看。

passages.original: Presently Peter sneezed--'Kertyschoo!'
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒彼得打咗個噴嚏——「阿嚏!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒彼得打了個噴嚏——「阿嚏!」

passages.original: Mr. McGregor was after him in no time.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生即刻追咗上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生立刻追了上去。

passages.original: And tried to put his foot upon Peter, who jumped out of a window, upsetting three plants.
passages.vernacular: 仲想用腳踩彼得,彼得從窗子跳咗出去,撞翻咗三盆植物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還想用腳踩彼得,彼得從窗子跳了出去,撞翻了三盆植物。

passages.original: The window was too small for Mr. McGregor, and he was tired of running after Peter.
passages.vernacular: 窗子對麥克格雷格先生來講太小喇,佢都追彼得追累喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子對麥克格雷格先生來說太小了,他也追彼得追累了。

passages.original: He went back to his work.
passages.vernacular: 佢回去幹活喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回去幹活了。

passages.original: Peter sat down to rest; he was out of breath and trembling with fright, and he had not the least idea which way to go.
passages.vernacular: 彼得坐下嚟休息;佢上氣不接下氣,嚇得發抖,完全唔知道該往邊個方向走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得坐下來休息;他上氣不接下氣,嚇得發抖,完全不知道該往哪個方向走。

passages.original: Also he was very damp with sitting in that can.
passages.vernacular: 而且因為坐喺嗰個罐子裡,佢全身濕透喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且因為坐在那個罐子裡,他全身濕透了。

passages.original: After a time he began to wander about, going lippity--lippity--not very fast, and looking all round.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,佢開始四處漫步,蹦蹦跳跳地走,不太快,四下張望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,他開始四處漫步,蹦蹦跳跳地走,不太快,四下張望。

passages.original: He found a door in a wall; but it was locked, and there was no room for a fat little rabbit to squeeze underneath.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現牆上有一扇門;不過鎖住,而且門下面冇地方能讓一隻胖胖嘅小兔子擠過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發現牆上有一扇門;可是鎖著,而且門下面沒有地方能讓一隻胖胖的小兔子擠過去。

passages.original: An old mouse was running in and out over the stone doorstep, carrying peas and beans to her family in the wood.
passages.vernacular: 一隻老鼠喺石頭門檻上跑進跑出,畀樹林裡佢嘅家人搬豌豆同豆子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻老鼠在石頭門檻上跑進跑出,給樹林裡她的家人搬豌豆和豆子。

passages.original: Peter asked her the way to the gate, but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not answer.
passages.vernacular: 彼得問佢去大門嘅路,不過佢嘴裡含住一顆好大嘅豌豆,冇法回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得問她去大門的路,可是她嘴裡含著一顆很大的豌豆,沒法回答。

passages.original: She only shook her head at him.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係朝佢搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是朝他搖搖頭。

passages.original: Peter began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 彼得開始哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得開始哭了。

passages.original: Then he tried to find his way straight across the garden, but he became more and more puzzled.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢試住直接穿過園子找路,不過佢越嚟越糊塗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他試著直接穿過園子找路,可是他越來越糊塗。

passages.original: Presently, he came to a pond where Mr. McGregor filled his water-cans.
passages.vernacular: 不久,佢嚟到一個池塘,麥克格雷格先生喺嗰度灌佢嘅水罐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,他來到一個池塘,麥克格雷格先生在那裡灌他的水罐。

passages.original: A white cat was staring at some gold-fish, she sat very, very still, but now and then the tip of her tail twitched as if it were alive.
passages.vernacular: 一隻白貓正盯住啲金魚,佢坐得好好靜,只係偶爾尾巴尖抽動一下,好像佢係活嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻白貓正盯著一些金魚,她坐得非常非常靜,只是偶爾尾巴尖抽動一下,好像它是活的。

passages.original: Peter thought it best to go away without speaking to her; he had heard about cats from his cousin, little Benjamin Bunny.
passages.vernacular: 彼得覺得最好唔好同佢講話就走開;佢從堂弟小班傑明兔嗰度聽講過貓嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得覺得最好不要同她說話就走開;他從堂弟小班傑明兔那裡聽說過貓的事。

passages.original: He went back towards the tool-shed, but suddenly, quite close to him, he heard the noise of a hoe--scr-r-ritch, scratch, scratch, scritch.
passages.vernacular: 佢朝工具棚走回去,不過突然,就喺佢附近,佢聽到鋤頭嘅聲音——嚓、嚓、嚓、嚓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他朝工具棚走回去,可是突然,就在他附近,他聽到鋤頭的聲音——嚓、嚓、嚓、嚓。

passages.original: Peter scuttered underneath the bushes.
passages.vernacular: 彼得急忙鑽到灌木叢下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得急忙鑽到灌木叢下面。

passages.original: But presently, as nothing happened, he came out, and climbed upon a wheelbarrow and peeped over.
passages.vernacular: 不過過咗一會兒,乜嘢都冇發生,佢就出嚟,爬上一輛獨輪手推車往外窺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是過了一會兒,什麼也沒發生,他就出來,爬上一輛獨輪手推車往外窺看。

passages.original: The first thing he saw was Mr. McGregor hoeing onions.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇見嘅第一樣嘢,係麥克格雷格先生喺鋤洋蔥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看見的第一樣東西,是麥克格雷格先生在鋤洋蔥。

passages.original: His back was turned towards Peter, and beyond him was the gate!
passages.vernacular: 佢背對住彼得,而喺佢後面就係大門!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他背對著彼得,而在他後面就是大門!

passages.original: Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started running as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some black-currant bushes.
passages.vernacular: 彼得好安靜地從手推車上下嚟;開始盡佢所能地快跑,沿住黑加侖叢後面嘅一條直路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得非常安靜地從手推車上下來;開始盡他所能地快跑,沿著黑加侖叢後面的一條直路。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor caught sight of him at the corner, but Peter did not care.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生喺拐角處瞥見咗佢,可彼得不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生在拐角處瞥見了他,可彼得不在乎。

passages.original: He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood outside the garden.
passages.vernacular: 佢從大門底下鑽咗出去,終於安全地到咗園子外面嘅樹林裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從大門底下鑽了出去,終於安全地到了園子外面的樹林裡。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor hung up the little jacket and the shoes for a scare-crow to frighten the blackbirds.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生把嗰件小外套同鞋子掛起嚟當稻草人,嚇唬黑鸝鳥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生把那件小外套和鞋子掛起來當稻草人,嚇唬黑鸝鳥。

passages.original: Peter never stopped running or looked behind him till he got home to the big fir-tree.
passages.vernacular: 彼得一直跑,冇停下,都冇回頭睇,直到回到嗰棵大冷杉樹下嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得一直跑,沒有停下,也沒有回頭看,直到回到那棵大冷杉樹下的家。

passages.original: He was so tired that he flopped down upon the nice soft sand on the floor of the rabbit-hole and shut his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢累得撲倒喺兔子洞地面上嗰柔軟嘅沙子上,閉上咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他累得撲倒在兔子洞地面上那柔軟的沙子上,閉上了眼睛。

passages.original: His mother was busy cooking; she wondered what he had done with his clothes.
passages.vernacular: 佢母親正忙住做飯;佢納悶佢把衣服點喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他母親正忙著做飯;她納悶他把衣服怎麼了。

passages.original: It was the second little jacket and pair of shoes that Peter had lost in a fortnight!
passages.vernacular: 呢個係彼得兩個星期裡丟嘅第二件小外套同第二雙鞋子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是彼得兩個星期裡丟的第二件小外套和第二雙鞋子!

passages.original: I am sorry to say that Peter was not very well during the evening.
passages.vernacular: 我好遺憾地講,嗰天晚上彼得不太舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很遺憾地說,那天晚上彼得不太舒服。

passages.original: His mother put him to bed, and made some camomile tea; and she gave a dose of it to Peter!
passages.vernacular: 佢母親把佢放到床上,煮咗些甘菊茶;佢還畀彼得餵咗一劑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他母親把他放到床上,煮了些甘菊茶;她還給彼得餵了一劑!

passages.original: 'One table-spoonful to be taken at bed-time.'
passages.vernacular: 「瞓前服一湯匙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「睡前服一湯匙。」

passages.original: But Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and blackberries for supper.
passages.vernacular: 不過福洛西、莫洛西同棉尾巴晚飯食嘅係麵包、牛奶同黑莓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是福洛西、莫洛西和棉尾巴晚飯吃的是麵包、牛奶和黑莓。

chapters.title: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny 班傑明兔的故事

passages.original: CH One morning a little rabbit sat on a bank.
passages.vernacular: 一天早晨,一隻小兔子坐喺一個土坡上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天早晨,一隻小兔子坐在一個土坡上。

passages.original: He pricked his ears and listened to the trit-trot, trit-trot of a pony.
passages.vernacular: 佢豎起耳朵,聽住一匹小馬嘚嘚、嘚嘚嘅蹄聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他豎起耳朵,聽著一匹小馬嘚嘚、嘚嘚的蹄聲。

passages.original: A gig was coming along the road; it was driven by Mr. McGregor, and beside him sat Mrs. McGregor in her best bonnet.
passages.vernacular: 一輛雙輪馬車沿住路過嚟;趕車嘅係麥克格雷格先生,佢旁邊坐住戴住最好嘅帽子嘅麥克格雷格太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一輛雙輪馬車沿著路過來;趕車的是麥克格雷格先生,他旁邊坐著戴著最好的帽子的麥克格雷格太太。

passages.original: As soon as they had passed, little Benjamin Bunny slid down into the road, and set off--with a hop, skip, and a jump--to call upon his relations, who lived in the wood at the back of Mr. McGregor's garden.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一過去,小班傑明兔就滑下到路上,蹦蹦跳跳地出發喇——一蹦、一跳、一躍——去拜訪佢嘅親戚,佢哋住喺麥克格雷格先生園子後面嘅樹林裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們一過去,小班傑明兔就滑下到路上,蹦蹦跳跳地出發了——一蹦、一跳、一躍——去拜訪他的親戚,他們住在麥克格雷格先生園子後面的樹林裡。

passages.original: That wood was full of rabbit holes; and in the neatest, sandiest hole of all lived Benjamin's aunt and his cousins--Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
passages.vernacular: 嗰片樹林裡全係兔子洞;而喺最整潔、沙地最多嘅嗰個洞裡,住班傑明嘅姑媽同佢嘅堂兄弟姐妹——福洛西、莫洛西、棉尾巴同彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那片樹林裡全是兔子洞;而在最整潔、沙地最多的那個洞裡,住著班傑明的姑媽和他的堂兄弟姐妹——福洛西、莫洛西、棉尾巴和彼得。

passages.original: Old Mrs. Rabbit was a widow; she earned her living by knitting rabbit-wool mittens and muffatees (I once bought a pair at a bazaar).
passages.vernacular: 老兔太太係個寡婦;佢靠織兔毛手套同護腕謀生(我有一次喺義賣會上買過一雙)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老兔太太是個寡婦;她靠織兔毛手套和護腕謀生(我有一次在義賣會上買過一雙)。

passages.original: She also sold herbs, and rosemary tea, and rabbit-tobacco (which is what we call lavender).
passages.vernacular: 佢仲賣草藥、迷迭香茶同兔子煙草(都就係我哋所講嘅薰衣草)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還賣草藥、迷迭香茶和兔子煙草(也就是我們所說的薰衣草)。

passages.original: Little Benjamin did not very much want to see his Aunt.
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明不太想見佢嘅姑媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明不太想見他的姑媽。

passages.original: He came round the back of the fir-tree, and nearly tumbled upon the top of his Cousin Peter.
passages.vernacular: 佢繞到冷杉樹嘅後面,差點摔喺佢堂兄彼得身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他繞到冷杉樹的後面,差點摔在他堂兄彼得身上。

passages.original: Peter was sitting by himself.
passages.vernacular: 彼得獨自坐住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得獨自坐著。

passages.original: He looked poorly, and was dressed in a red cotton pocket-handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟病懨懨嘅,身上裹住一條紅棉布手帕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來病懨懨的,身上裹著一條紅棉布手帕。

passages.original: "Peter," said little Benjamin, in a whisper, "who has got your clothes?"
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」小班傑明低聲講,「邊個攞咗你嘅衣服?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」小班傑明低聲說,「誰拿了你的衣服?」

passages.original: Peter replied, "The scarecrow in Mr. McGregor's garden," and described how he had been chased about the garden, and had dropped his shoes and coat.
passages.vernacular: 彼得回答:「麥克格雷格先生園子裡嘅稻草人,」並描述咗佢點樣被追住喺園子裡跑,點樣丟咗鞋子同外套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得回答:「麥克格雷格先生園子裡的稻草人,」並描述了他怎樣被追著在園子裡跑,怎樣丟了鞋子和外套。

passages.original: Little Benjamin sat down beside his cousin and assured him that Mr. McGregor had gone out in a gig, and Mrs. McGregor also; and certainly for the day, because she was wearing her best bonnet.
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明喺堂兄身邊坐下,向佢保證麥克格雷格先生已經坐馬車出去喇,麥克格雷格太太都去喇;而且肯定係出去一整天,因為佢戴住佢最好嘅帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明在堂兄身邊坐下,向他保證麥克格雷格先生已經坐馬車出去了,麥克格雷格太太也去了;而且肯定是出去一整天,因為她戴著她最好的帽子。

passages.original: Peter said he hoped that it would rain.
passages.vernacular: 彼得講佢希望下雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得說他希望下雨。

passages.original: At this point old Mrs. Rabbit's voice was heard inside the rabbit hole, calling: "Cotton-tail!
passages.vernacular: 呢陣老兔太太嘅聲音從兔子洞裡傳出嚟,叫住:「棉尾巴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時老兔太太的聲音從兔子洞裡傳出來,叫著:「棉尾巴!

passages.original: Cotton-tail! fetch some more camomile!"
passages.vernacular: 棉尾巴!再去攞些甘菊嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 棉尾巴!再去拿些甘菊來!」

passages.original: Peter said he thought he might feel better if he went for a walk.
passages.vernacular: 彼得講佢想如果出去走走,或者會好些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得說他想如果出去走走,也許會好些。

passages.original: They went away hand in hand, and got upon the flat top of the wall at the bottom of the wood.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋手拉手走開,爬到樹林底部嗰堵牆嘅平頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們手拉手走開,爬到樹林底部那堵牆的平頂上。

passages.original: From here they looked down into Mr. McGregor's garden.
passages.vernacular: 從呢度佢哋往下睇麥克格雷格先生嘅園子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從這裡他們往下看麥克格雷格先生的園子。

passages.original: Peter's coat and shoes were plainly to be seen upon the scarecrow, topped with an old tam-o'-shanter of Mr. McGregor's.
passages.vernacular: 彼得嘅外套同鞋子清清楚楚地穿喺稻草人身上,稻草人頭上仲戴住麥克格雷格先生嘅一頂舊蘇格蘭圓帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得的外套和鞋子清清楚楚地穿在稻草人身上,稻草人頭上還戴著麥克格雷格先生的一頂舊蘇格蘭圓帽。

passages.original: Little Benjamin said: "It spoils people's clothes to squeeze under a gate; the proper way to get in is to climb down a pear-tree."
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明講:「從大門底下擠進去會弄壞人嘅衣服;正確嘅進去辦法係順住梨樹爬下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明說:「從大門底下擠進去會弄壞人的衣服;正確的進去辦法是順著梨樹爬下去。」

passages.original: Peter fell down head first; but it was of no consequence, as the bed below was newly raked and quite soft.
passages.vernacular: 彼得頭朝下摔咗下去;不過冇關係,因為下面嘅花壇剛耙過,相當柔軟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得頭朝下摔了下去;不過沒關係,因為下面的花壇剛耙過,相當柔軟。

passages.original: It had been sown with lettuces.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度種嘅係萵苣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡種的是萵苣。

passages.original: They left a great many odd little footmarks all over the bed, especially little Benjamin, who was wearing clogs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺花壇上留下咗許多古怪嘅小腳印,特別係小班傑明,佢穿住木底鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在花壇上留下了許多古怪的小腳印,特別是小班傑明,他穿著木底鞋。

passages.original: Little Benjamin said that the first thing to be done was to get back Peter's clothes, in order that they might be able to use the pocket-handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明講,首先要做嘅係把彼得嘅衣服攞回嚟,咁樣佢哋就可以用嗰條手帕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明說,首先要做的是把彼得的衣服拿回來,這樣他們就可以用那條手帕了。

passages.original: They took them off the scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把衣服從稻草人身上脫下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把衣服從稻草人身上脫下來。

passages.original: There had been rain during the night; there was water in the shoes, and the coat was somewhat shrunk.
passages.vernacular: 夜裡下過雨;鞋子裡有水,外套都有點縮水喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜裡下過雨;鞋子裡有水,外套也有點縮水了。

passages.original: Benjamin tried on the tam-o'-shanter, but it was too big for him.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明試戴咗嗰頂圓帽,不過對佢太大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明試戴了那頂圓帽,可是對他太大了。

passages.original: Then he suggested that they should fill the pocket-handkerchief with onions, as a little present for his Aunt.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢建議佢哋用手帕裝滿洋蔥,畀佢姑媽當一份小禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他建議他們用手帕裝滿洋蔥,給他姑媽當一份小禮物。

passages.original: Peter did not seem to be enjoying himself; he kept hearing noises.
passages.vernacular: 彼得似乎玩得不開心;佢總是聽見聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得似乎玩得不開心;他總是聽見聲音。

passages.original: Benjamin, on the contrary, was perfectly at home, and ate a lettuce leaf.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明則相反,佢完全像喺家裡一樣,食咗一片萵苣葉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明則相反,他完全像在家裡一樣,吃了一片萵苣葉。

passages.original: He said that he was in the habit of coming to the garden with his father to get lettuces for their Sunday dinner.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢常同爸爸嚟呢個園子,為佢哋嘅星期日晚飯弄萵苣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他常和爸爸來這個園子,為他們的星期日晚飯弄萵苣。

passages.original: (The name of little Benjamin's papa was old Mr. Benjamin Bunny.)
passages.vernacular: (小班傑明嘅爸爸叫老班傑明·兔先生。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (小班傑明的爸爸叫老班傑明·兔先生。)

passages.original: The lettuces certainly were very fine.
passages.vernacular: 萵苣確實好棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 萵苣確實很棒。

passages.original: Peter did not eat anything; he said he should like to go home.
passages.vernacular: 彼得乜嘢都冇食;佢講佢想回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得什麼也沒吃;他說他想回家。

passages.original: Presently he dropped half the onions.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢掉咗一半嘅洋蔥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他掉了一半的洋蔥。

passages.original: Little Benjamin said that it was not possible to get back up the pear-tree with a load of vegetables.
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明講,帶住一大堆蔬菜係冇法爬回梨樹上去嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明說,帶著一大堆蔬菜是沒法爬回梨樹上去的。

passages.original: He led the way boldly towards the other end of the garden.
passages.vernacular: 佢大膽地領頭朝園子嘅另一頭走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他大膽地領頭朝園子的另一頭走去。

passages.original: They went along a little walk on planks, under a sunny, red brick wall.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋沿住一條木板小路走,走喺一堵陽光照耀嘅紅磚牆下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沿著一條木板小路走,走在一堵陽光照耀的紅磚牆下。

passages.original: The mice sat on their doorsteps cracking cherry-stones; they winked at Peter Rabbit and little Benjamin Bunny.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠哋坐喺自家門檻上磕櫻桃核;牠哋對彼得兔同小班傑明兔眨眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠們坐在自家門檻上磕櫻桃核;牠們對彼得兔和小班傑明兔眨眼睛。

passages.original: Presently Peter let the pocket-handkerchief go again.
passages.vernacular: 不久彼得又讓手帕掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久彼得又讓手帕掉了。

passages.original: They got amongst flower-pots, and frames, and tubs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走到花盆、溫床框同木桶中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們走到花盆、溫床框和木桶中間。

passages.original: Peter heard noises worse than ever; his eyes were as big as lolly-pops!
passages.vernacular: 彼得聽到嘅聲音比以前更糟;佢嘅眼睛瞪得像棒棒糖一樣大!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得聽到的聲音比以前更糟;他的眼睛瞪得像棒棒糖一樣大!

passages.original: He was a step or two in front of his cousin when he suddenly stopped.
passages.vernacular: 佢走喺堂兄前面一兩步時,突然停住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走在堂兄前面一兩步時,突然停住了。

passages.original: This is what those little rabbits saw round that corner!
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰兩隻小兔子喺嗰個拐角睇見嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那兩隻小兔子在那個拐角看見的!

passages.original: Little Benjamin took one look, and then, in half a minute less than no time, he hid himself and Peter and the onions underneath a large basket....
passages.vernacular: 小班傑明睇咗一眼,然後,比眨眼仲快,佢把自己、彼得同洋蔥都藏到咗一個大籃子底下……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小班傑明看了一眼,然後,比眨眼還快,他把自己、彼得和洋蔥都藏到了一個大籃子底下……

passages.original: The cat got up and stretched herself, and came and sniffed at the basket.
passages.vernacular: 貓站起嚟,伸咗個懶腰,走過嚟嗅咗嗅籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓站起來,伸了個懶腰,走過來嗅了嗅籃子。

passages.original: Perhaps she liked the smell of onions!
passages.vernacular: 或者佢鍾意洋蔥嘅味道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她喜歡洋蔥的味道!

passages.original: Anyway, she sat down upon the top of the basket.
passages.vernacular: 總之,佢坐喺咗籃子嘅頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,她坐在了籃子的頂上。

passages.original: She sat there for five hours.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺嗰度坐咗五個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在那裡坐了五個小時。

passages.original: I cannot draw you a picture of Peter and Benjamin underneath the basket, because it was quite dark, and because the smell of onions was fearful; it made Peter Rabbit and little Benjamin cry.
passages.vernacular: 我冇法畀你哋畫彼得同班傑明喺籃子底下嘅樣子,因為嗰度面好黑,而且洋蔥嘅味道可怕極喇;佢讓彼得兔同小班傑明兔都哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒法給你們畫彼得和班傑明在籃子底下的樣子,因為那裡面很黑,而且洋蔥的味道可怕極了;它讓彼得兔和小班傑明兔都哭了。

passages.original: The sun got round behind the wood, and it was quite late in the afternoon; but still the cat sat upon the basket.
passages.vernacular: 太陽轉到樹林後面,已經係下午好晚喇;不過貓仍然坐喺籃子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽轉到樹林後面,已經是下午很晚了;可是貓仍然坐在籃子上。

passages.original: At length there was a pitter-patter, pitter-patter, and some bits of mortar fell from the wall above.
passages.vernacular: 終於,響起咗啪嗒啪嗒、啪嗒啪嗒嘅聲音,幾塊灰泥從上面嘅牆上掉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於,響起了啪嗒啪嗒、啪嗒啪嗒的聲音,幾塊灰泥從上面的牆上掉了下來。

passages.original: The cat looked up and saw old Mr. Benjamin Bunny prancing along the top of the wall of the upper terrace.
passages.vernacular: 貓抬頭睇,睇見老班傑明·兔先生正沿住上層露台牆頂蹦蹦跳跳地走嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓抬頭看,看見老班傑明·兔先生正沿著上層露台牆頂蹦蹦跳跳地走來。

passages.original: He was smoking a pipe of rabbit-tobacco, and had a little switch in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺抽一斗兔子煙草,手裡攞住一根小鞭子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在抽一斗兔子煙草,手裡拿著一根小鞭子。

passages.original: He was looking for his son.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺找佢嘅兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在找他的兒子。

passages.original: Old Mr. Bunny had no opinion whatever of cats.
passages.vernacular: 老兔先生對貓根本冇乜嘢好感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老兔先生對貓根本沒有什麼好感。

passages.original: He took a tremendous jump off the top of the wall on to the top of the cat, and cuffed it off the basket, and kicked it into the greenhouse, scratching off a handful of fur.
passages.vernacular: 佢從牆頭猛地一跳,跳到貓嘅背上,一巴掌把佢從籃子上打下嚟,又一腳把佢踢進咗溫室,仲抓下咗一把毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從牆頭猛地一跳,跳到貓的背上,一巴掌把她從籃子上打下來,又一腳把她踢進了溫室,還抓下了一把毛。

passages.original: The cat was too much surprised to scratch back.
passages.vernacular: 貓太食驚喇,冇抓回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓太吃驚了,沒有抓回去。

passages.original: When old Mr. Bunny had driven the cat into the greenhouse, he locked the door.
passages.vernacular: 老兔先生把貓趕進溫室後,把門鎖上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老兔先生把貓趕進溫室後,把門鎖上了。

passages.original: Then he came back to the basket and took out his son Benjamin by the ears, and whipped him with the little switch.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢回到籃子旁,抓住耳朵把佢兒子班傑明拎出嚟,用小鞭子抽佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他回到籃子旁,抓著耳朵把他兒子班傑明拎出來,用小鞭子抽他。

passages.original: Then he took out his nephew Peter.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把佢嘅侄子彼得拎出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他把他的侄子彼得拎出來。

passages.original: Then he took out the handkerchief of onions, and marched out of the garden.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢攞出嗰條裝住洋蔥嘅手帕,大步走出咗園子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他拿出那條裝著洋蔥的手帕,大步走出了園子。

passages.original: When Mr. McGregor returned about half an hour later he observed several things which perplexed him.
passages.vernacular: 大約半個小時後麥克格雷格先生回嚟時,佢發現咗好幾件讓佢困惑嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約半個小時後麥克格雷格先生回來時,他發現了好幾件讓他困惑的事。

passages.original: It looked as though some person had been walking all over the garden in a pair of clogs--only the footmarks were too ridiculously little!
passages.vernacular: 睇起嚟好像有人穿住一雙木底鞋喺整個園子裡走過——只係腳印小得可笑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看起來好像有人穿著一雙木底鞋在整個園子裡走過——只是腳印小得可笑!

passages.original: Also he could not understand how the cat could have managed to shut herself up inside the greenhouse, locking the door upon the outside.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢都弄不明白,貓點能把自己關喺溫室裡,從外面鎖上門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他也弄不明白,貓怎麼能把自己關在溫室裡,從外面鎖上門。

passages.original: When Peter got home his mother forgave him, because she was so glad to see that he had found his shoes and coat.
passages.vernacular: 彼得回到家時,佢母親原諒咗佢,因為佢太高興睇到佢找回咗鞋子同外套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得回到家時,他母親原諒了他,因為她太高興看到他找回了鞋子和外套。

passages.original: Cotton-tail and Peter folded up the pocket-handkerchief, and old Mrs. Rabbit strung up the onions and hung them from the kitchen ceiling, with the bunches of herbs and the rabbit-tobacco.
passages.vernacular: 棉尾巴同彼得把手帕疊好,老兔太太把洋蔥串起嚟,連同成束嘅草藥同兔子煙草一起,掛喺廚房天花板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 棉尾巴和彼得把手帕疊好,老兔太太把洋蔥串起來,連同成束的草藥和兔子煙草一起,掛在廚房天花板上。

chapters.title: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin 松鼠納特金的故事

passages.original: CH This is a Tale about a tail--a tail that belonged to a little red squirrel, and his name was Nutkin.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一個關於尾巴嘅故事——一條屬於一隻小紅松鼠嘅尾巴,佢嘅名字叫納特金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一個關於尾巴的故事——一條屬於一隻小紅松鼠的尾巴,他的名字叫納特金。

passages.original: He had a brother called Twinkleberry, and a great many cousins: they lived in a wood at the edge of a lake.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一個弟弟叫閃亮莓,仲有許多堂兄弟:佢哋住喺湖邊嘅樹林裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一個弟弟叫閃亮莓,還有許多堂兄弟:他們住在湖邊的樹林裡。

passages.original: In the middle of the lake there is an island covered with trees and nut bushes; and amongst those trees stands a hollow oak-tree, which is the house of an owl who is called Old Brown.
passages.vernacular: 湖中央有一座島,長滿咗樹同堅果灌木;喺嗰啲樹中間,有一棵空心橡樹,係一隻叫老布朗嘅貓頭鷹嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湖中央有一座島,長滿了樹和堅果灌木;在那些樹中間,有一棵空心橡樹,是一隻叫老布朗的貓頭鷹的家。

passages.original: One autumn when the nuts were ripe, and the leaves on the hazel bushes were golden and green--Nutkin and Twinkleberry and all the other little squirrels came out of the wood, and down to the edge of the lake.
passages.vernacular: 一個秋天,堅果成熟喇,榛樹叢嘅葉子係金黃同綠色嘅——納特金、閃亮莓同所有其他小松鼠從樹林裡出嚟,嚟到湖邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個秋天,堅果成熟了,榛樹叢的葉子是金黃和綠色的——納特金、閃亮莓和所有其他小松鼠從樹林裡出來,來到湖邊。

passages.original: They made little rafts out of twigs, and they paddled away over the water to Owl Island to gather nuts.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋用細樹枝做咗小木筏,划住槳穿過水面,去貓頭鷹島採堅果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們用細樹枝做了小木筏,划著槳穿過水面,去貓頭鷹島採堅果。

passages.original: Each squirrel had a little sack and a large oar, and spread out his tail for a sail.
passages.vernacular: 每隻松鼠有一個小袋子同一把大槳,並展開尾巴當帆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每隻松鼠有一個小袋子和一把大槳,並展開尾巴當帆。

passages.original: They also took with them an offering of three fat mice as a present for Old Brown, and put them down upon his door-step.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仲帶咗三隻肥老鼠作為獻畀老布朗嘅禮物,放喺佢嘅門階上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們還帶了三隻肥老鼠作為獻給老布朗的禮物,放在他的門階上。

passages.original: Then Twinkleberry and the other little squirrels each made a low bow, and said politely--
passages.vernacular: 然後閃亮莓同其他小松鼠每個都鞠咗一個躬,客氣地講——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後閃亮莓和其他小松鼠每個都鞠了一個躬,客氣地說——

passages.original: "Old Mr. Brown, will you favour us with permission to gather nuts upon your island?"
passages.vernacular: 「老布朗先生,您能允許我哋喺您嘅島上採堅果嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「老布朗先生,您能允許我們在您的島上採堅果嗎?」

passages.original: But Nutkin was excessively impertinent in his manners.
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金舉止極其無禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金舉止極其無禮。

passages.original: He bobbed up and down like a little red cherry, singing--
passages.vernacular: 佢像一顆小紅櫻桃一樣上下蹦跳,唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他像一顆小紅櫻桃一樣上下蹦跳,唱著——

passages.original: "Riddle me, riddle me, rot-tot-tote!
passages.vernacular: 「猜謎,猜謎,嘟嘟嘟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「猜謎,猜謎,嘟嘟嘟!

passages.original: A little wee man, in a red red coat!
passages.vernacular: 一個小小人,穿住紅紅嘅外套!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個小小人,穿著紅紅的外套!

passages.original: A staff in his hand, and a stone in his throat; If you'll tell me this riddle, I'll give you a groat."
passages.vernacular: 手裡攞著手杖,喉嚨裡有塊石頭;你要係猜出呢個謎,我就畀你一個格羅特。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 手裡拿著手杖,喉嚨裡有塊石頭;你要是猜出這個謎,我就給你一個格羅特。」

passages.original: Now this riddle is as old as the hills; Mr. Brown paid no attention whatever to Nutkin.
passages.vernacular: 呢個謎語老得同山一樣古老;布朗先生根本不理睬納特金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個謎語老得和山一樣古老;布朗先生根本不理睬納特金。

passages.original: He shut his eyes obstinately and went to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢固執地閉上眼睛,瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他固執地閉上眼睛,睡著了。

passages.original: The squirrels filled their little sacks with nuts, and sailed away home in the evening.
passages.vernacular: 松鼠哋把小袋子裝滿咗堅果,傍晚乘船回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 松鼠們把小袋子裝滿了堅果,傍晚乘船回家了。

passages.original: But next morning they all came back again to Owl Island; and Twinkleberry and the others brought a fine fat mole, and laid it on the stone in front of Old Brown's doorway, and said--
passages.vernacular: 不過第二天早晨佢哋又都回到貓頭鷹島;閃亮莓同其他松鼠帶嚟咗一隻漂亮嘅肥鼴鼠,放喺老布朗門口前嘅石頭上,講——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是第二天早晨他們又都回到貓頭鷹島;閃亮莓和其他松鼠帶來了一隻漂亮的肥鼴鼠,放在老布朗門口前的石頭上,說——

passages.original: "Mr. Brown, will you favour us with your gracious permission to gather some more nuts?"
passages.vernacular: 「布朗先生,您能賜予我哋您仁慈嘅許可,再採啲堅果嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「布朗先生,您能賜予我們您仁慈的許可,再採一些堅果嗎?」

passages.original: But Nutkin, who had no respect, began to dance up and down, tickling old Mr. Brown with a nettle and singing--
passages.vernacular: 不過毫無敬意嘅納特金,開始上下跳舞,用一棵蕁麻去撓老布朗先生,唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是毫無敬意的納特金,開始上下跳舞,用一棵蕁麻去撓老布朗先生,唱著——

passages.original: "Old Mr. B!
passages.vernacular: 「老布先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「老布先生!

passages.original: Riddle-me-ree!
passages.vernacular: 猜謎猜謎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猜謎猜謎!

passages.original: Hitty Pitty within the wall, Hitty Pitty without the wall; If you touch Hitty Pitty, Hitty Pitty will bite you!"
passages.vernacular: 牆內有個嘻皮蒂,牆外有個嘻皮蒂;你要係碰咗嘻皮蒂,嘻皮蒂就咬你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牆內有個嘻皮蒂,牆外有個嘻皮蒂;你要是碰了嘻皮蒂,嘻皮蒂就咬你!」

passages.original: Mr. Brown woke up suddenly and carried the mole into his house.
passages.vernacular: 布朗先生突然醒喇,把鼴鼠攞進佢嘅屋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布朗先生突然醒了,把鼴鼠拿進他的屋裡。

passages.original: He shut the door in Nutkin's face.
passages.vernacular: 佢當住納特金嘅面關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他當著納特金的面關上了門。

passages.original: Presently a little thread of blue smoke from a wood fire came up from the top of the tree, and Nutkin peeped through the key-hole and sang--
passages.vernacular: 不久,一縷藍色嘅細煙,從樹頂上嘅柴火中升起,納特金從鑰匙孔窺視,唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,一縷藍色的細煙,從樹頂上的柴火中升起,納特金從鑰匙孔窺視,唱著——

passages.original: "A house full, a hole full!
passages.vernacular: 「一屋子,一洞子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一屋子,一洞子!

passages.original: And you cannot gather a bowl-full!"
passages.vernacular: 你一碗都採不滿!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一碗也採不滿!」

passages.original: The squirrels searched for nuts all over the island and filled their little sacks.
passages.vernacular: 松鼠哋搜遍整座島找堅果,把小袋子裝滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 松鼠們搜遍整座島找堅果,把小袋子裝滿。

passages.original: But Nutkin gathered oak-apples--yellow and scarlet--and sat upon a beech-stump playing marbles, and watching the door of old Mr. Brown.
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金採嘅係橡樹蟲癭——黃色同猩紅色嘅——坐喺一個山毛櫸樹樁上玩彈珠,睇住老布朗先生嘅門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金採的是橡樹蟲癭——黃色和猩紅色的——坐在一個山毛櫸樹樁上玩彈珠,看著老布朗先生的門。

passages.original: On the third day the squirrels got up very early and went fishing; they caught seven fat minnows as a present for Old Brown.
passages.vernacular: 第三天,松鼠哋起得好早,去釣魚;佢哋釣到七條肥小魚,作為畀老布朗嘅禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第三天,松鼠們起得很早,去釣魚;他們釣到七條肥小魚,作為給老布朗的禮物。

passages.original: They paddled over the lake and landed under a crooked chestnut tree on Owl Island.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋划過湖面,喺貓頭鷹島上一棵彎曲嘅栗樹下登岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們划過湖面,在貓頭鷹島上一棵彎曲的栗樹下登岸。

passages.original: Twinkleberry and six other little squirrels each carried a fat minnow; but Nutkin, who had no nice manners, brought no present at all.
passages.vernacular: 閃亮莓同另外六隻小松鼠每個都提住一條肥魚;不過冇好禮貌嘅納特金,乜嘢禮物都冇帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閃亮莓和另外六隻小松鼠每個都提著一條肥魚;可是沒有好禮貌的納特金,什麼禮物也沒帶。

passages.original: He ran in front, singing--
passages.vernacular: 佢跑喺前面,唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跑在前面,唱著——

passages.original: "The man in the wilderness said to me, 'How many strawberries grow in the sea?'
passages.vernacular: 「荒野裡嘅人對我講:『海裡長多少草莓?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「荒野裡的人對我說:『海裡長多少草莓?』

passages.original: I answered him as I thought good-- 'As many red herrings as grow in the wood.'"
passages.vernacular: 我回答佢,我認為好嘅——『樹林裡長多少紅鯡魚,就長多少。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我回答他,我認為好的——『樹林裡長多少紅鯡魚,就長多少。』」

passages.original: But old Mr. Brown took no interest in riddles--not even when the answer was provided for him.
passages.vernacular: 不過老布朗先生對謎語不感興趣——即使連答案都畀佢喇,都不感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是老布朗先生對謎語不感興趣——即使連答案也給他了,也不感興趣。

passages.original: On the fourth day the squirrels brought a present of six fat beetles, which were as good as plums in plum-pudding for Old Brown.
passages.vernacular: 第四天,松鼠哋帶嚟六隻肥甲蟲作為禮物,對老布朗來講就像李子布丁裡嘅李子一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第四天,松鼠們帶來六隻肥甲蟲作為禮物,對老布朗來說就像李子布丁裡的李子一樣好。

passages.original: Each beetle was wrapped up carefully in a dock-leaf, fastened with a pine-needle pin.
passages.vernacular: 每隻甲蟲都小心地用酸模葉包起嚟,用松針別住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每隻甲蟲都小心地用酸模葉包起來,用松針別著。

passages.original: But Nutkin sang as rudely as ever--
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金定係像以前一樣無禮地唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金還是像以前一樣無禮地唱著——

passages.original: "Old Mr. B! riddle-me-ree Flour of England, fruit of Spain, Met together in a shower of rain; Put in a bag tied round with a string, If you'll tell me this riddle, I'll give you a ring!"
passages.vernacular: 「老布先生!猜謎猜謎,英格蘭嘅麵粉,西班牙嘅水果,喺一場雨裡相遇;放進一個袋子,用繩子紮起嚟,你要係猜出呢個謎,我就畀你一個戒指!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「老布先生!猜謎猜謎,英格蘭的麵粉,西班牙的水果,在一場雨裡相遇;放進一個袋子,用繩子紮起來,你要是猜出這個謎,我就給你一個戒指!」

passages.original: Which was ridiculous of Nutkin, because he had not got any ring to give to Old Brown.
passages.vernacular: 納特金咁樣講好荒唐,因為佢冇任何戒指可以畀老布朗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 納特金這樣說很荒唐,因為他沒有任何戒指可以給老布朗。

passages.original: The other squirrels hunted up and down the nut bushes; but Nutkin gathered robin's pincushions off a briar bush, and stuck them full of pine-needle pins.
passages.vernacular: 其他松鼠喺堅果灌木叢中上下搜尋;不過納特金從一叢野薔薇上採咗「知更鳥嘅針墊」,把佢哋插滿咗松針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他松鼠在堅果灌木叢中上下搜尋;可是納特金從一叢野薔薇上採了「知更鳥的針墊」,把它們插滿了松針。

passages.original: On the fifth day the squirrels brought a present of wild honey; it was so sweet and sticky that they licked their fingers as they put it down upon the stone.
passages.vernacular: 第五天,松鼠哋帶嚟咗野蜂蜜作為禮物;佢咁甜咁黏,佢哋把佢放喺石頭上時仲舔咗舔手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第五天,松鼠們帶來了野蜂蜜作為禮物;它那麼甜那麼黏,他們把它放在石頭上時還舔了舔手指。

passages.original: They had stolen it out of a bumble bees' nest on the tippitty top of the hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係從山頂上一個熊蜂窩裡偷嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們是從山頂上一個熊蜂窩裡偷來的。

passages.original: But Nutkin skipped up and down, singing--
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金上下跳躍,唱住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金上下跳躍,唱著——

passages.original: "Hum-a-bum! buzz! buzz!
passages.vernacular: 「嗡嗡嗡!嗡!嗡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗡嗡嗡!嗡!嗡!

passages.original: Hum-a-bum buzz!
passages.vernacular: 嗡嗡嗡嗡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗡嗡嗡嗡!

passages.original: As I went over Tipple-tine I met a flock of bonny swine; Some yellow-nacked, some yellow backed!
passages.vernacular: 我走過提普提山,遇到一群漂亮嘅豬;有嘅黃頸,有嘅黃背!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走過提普提山,遇到一群漂亮的豬;有的黃頸,有的黃背!

passages.original: They were the very bonniest swine That e'er went over Tipple-tine."
passages.vernacular: 牠哋係走過提普提山最漂亮嘅豬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們是走過提普提山最漂亮的豬。」

passages.original: Old Mr. Brown turned up his eyes in disgust at the impertinence of Nutkin.
passages.vernacular: 老布朗先生對納特金嘅無禮厭惡地翻起咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老布朗先生對納特金的無禮厭惡地翻起了眼睛。

passages.original: But he ate up the honey!
passages.vernacular: 不過佢把蜂蜜食喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是他把蜂蜜吃了!

passages.original: The squirrels filled their little sacks with nuts.
passages.vernacular: 松鼠哋把小袋子裝滿咗堅果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 松鼠們把小袋子裝滿了堅果。

passages.original: But Nutkin sat upon a big flat rock, and played ninepins with a crab apple and green fir-cones.
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金坐喺一塊大平石上,用一個酸蘋果同綠杉果玩九柱戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金坐在一塊大平石上,用一個酸蘋果和綠杉果玩九柱戲。

passages.original: On the sixth day, which was Saturday, the squirrels came again for the last time; they brought a new-laid egg in a little rush basket as a last parting present for Old Brown.
passages.vernacular: 第六天,係星期六,松鼠哋最後一次嚟;佢哋帶嚟咗一個剛下嘅蛋,放喺一個小燈芯草籃子裡,作為畀老布朗嘅最後一份告別禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第六天,是星期六,松鼠們最後一次來;他們帶來了一個剛下的蛋,放在一個小燈芯草籃子裡,作為給老布朗的最後一份告別禮物。

passages.original: But Nutkin ran in front laughing, and shouting--
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金跑喺前面,笑住喊住——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金跑在前面,笑著喊著——

passages.original: "Humpty Dumpty lies in the beck, With a white counterpane round his neck, Forty doctors and forty wrights, Cannot put Humpty Dumpty to rights!"
passages.vernacular: 「矮胖子躺喺小溪裡,脖子上圍住白被單,四十個醫生同四十個工匠,都冇法把矮胖子治好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「矮胖子躺在小溪裡,脖子上圍著白被單,四十個醫生和四十個工匠,也沒法把矮胖子治好!」

passages.original: Now old Mr. Brown took an interest in eggs; he opened one eye and shut it again.
passages.vernacular: 老布朗先生對蛋係有興趣嘅;佢睜開一隻眼睛又閉上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老布朗先生對蛋是有興趣的;他睜開一隻眼睛又閉上了。

passages.original: But still he did not speak.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢仍然冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是他仍然沒說話。

passages.original: Nutkin became more and more impertinent--
passages.vernacular: 納特金變得越嚟越無禮——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 納特金變得越來越無禮——

passages.original: "Old Mr. B!
passages.vernacular: 「老布先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「老布先生!

passages.original: Old Mr. B!
passages.vernacular: 老布先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老布先生!

passages.original: Hickamore, Hackamore, on the King's kitchen door; All the King's horses, and all the King's men, Couldn't drive Hickamore, Hackamore, Off the King's kitchen door."
passages.vernacular: 嘻嗨嘻嗨,喺國王嘅廚房門上;國王所有嘅馬同國王所有嘅人,都趕不走嘻嗨嘻嗨,從國王嘅廚房門上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘻嗨嘻嗨,在國王的廚房門上;國王所有的馬和國王所有的人,也趕不走嘻嗨嘻嗨,從國王的廚房門上。」

passages.original: Nutkin danced up and down like a sunbeam; but still Old Brown said nothing at all.
passages.vernacular: 納特金像一道陽光一樣上下跳舞;不過老布朗仍然乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 納特金像一道陽光一樣上下跳舞;可是老布朗仍然什麼也沒說。

passages.original: Nutkin began again--
passages.vernacular: 納特金又開始喇——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 納特金又開始了——

passages.original: "Arthur O'Bower has broken his band, He comes roaring up the land!
passages.vernacular: 「鮑爾嘅亞瑟弄斷咗帶子,咆哮住衝上陸地!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鮑爾的亞瑟弄斷了帶子,咆哮著衝上陸地!

passages.original: The King of Scots with all his power, Cannot turn Arthur of the Bower!"
passages.vernacular: 蘇格蘭國王用盡全力,都冇法轉回鮑爾嘅亞瑟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蘇格蘭國王用盡全力,也沒法轉回鮑爾的亞瑟!」

passages.original: Nutkin made a whirring noise to sound like the wind, and he took a running jump right onto the head of Old Brown!...
passages.vernacular: 納特金發出呼呼嘅聲音,像風聲一樣,然後佢助跑一跳,正好跳到咗老布朗嘅頭上!……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 納特金發出呼呼的聲音,像風聲一樣,然後他助跑一跳,正好跳到了老布朗的頭上!……

passages.original: Then all at once there was a flutterment and a scufflement and a loud "Squeak!"
passages.vernacular: 然後突然一陣撲騰同扭打,仲有一聲響亮嘅「吱!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後突然一陣撲騰和扭打,還有一聲響亮的「吱!」

passages.original: The other squirrels scuttered away into the bushes.
passages.vernacular: 其他松鼠急忙逃進灌木叢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他松鼠急忙逃進灌木叢。

passages.original: When they came back very cautiously, peeping round the tree--there was Old Brown sitting on his door-step, quite still, with his eyes closed, as if nothing had happened.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好小心地回嚟,繞住樹窺睇時——老布朗正坐喺佢嘅門階上,一動不動,閉住眼睛,好像乜嘢都冇發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們非常小心地回來,繞著樹窺看時——老布朗正坐在他的門階上,一動不動,閉著眼睛,好像什麼都沒發生。

passages.original: But Nutkin was in his waistcoat pocket!
passages.vernacular: 不過納特金喺佢嘅背心口袋裡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是納特金在他的背心口袋裡!

passages.original: This looks like the end of the story; but it isn't.
passages.vernacular: 呢個睇起嚟像係故事嘅結局;但其實唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這看起來像是故事的結局;但其實不是。

passages.original: Old Brown carried Nutkin into his house, and held him up by the tail, intending to skin him; but Nutkin pulled so very hard that his tail broke in two, and he dashed up the staircase and escaped out of the attic window.
passages.vernacular: 老布朗把納特金帶進屋裡,抓住佢嘅尾巴把佢提起嚟,打算把佢剝皮;不過納特金拚命一拉,佢嘅尾巴斷成咗兩截,佢衝上樓梯,從閣樓窗口逃咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老布朗把納特金帶進屋裡,抓著他的尾巴把他提起來,打算把他剝皮;可是納特金拚命一拉,他的尾巴斷成了兩截,他衝上樓梯,從閣樓窗口逃了出去。

passages.original: And to this day, if you meet Nutkin up a tree and ask him a riddle, he will throw sticks at you, and stamp his feet and scold, and shout--
passages.vernacular: 直到今日,如果你喺樹上遇見納特金,問佢一個謎語,佢會朝你扔樹枝,跺腳罵人,並大喊——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到今天,如果你在樹上遇見納特金,問他一個謎語,他會朝你扔樹枝,跺腳罵人,並大喊——

passages.original: "Cuck-cuck-cuck-cur-r-r-cuck-k-k!"
passages.vernacular: 「咕咕咕咕——嚕嚕嚕咕咕咕!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「咕咕咕咕——嚕嚕嚕咕咕咕!」

chapters.title: The Tale of Two Bad Mice 兩隻壞老鼠的故事

passages.original: CH ONCE upon a time there was a very beautiful doll's-house; it was red brick with white windows, and it had real muslin curtains and a front door and a chimney.
passages.vernacular: 從前有一座好漂亮嘅玩偶屋;佢係紅磚砌嘅,有白色嘅窗子,有真正嘅細棉布窗簾、一扇前門同一個煙囪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有一座非常漂亮的玩偶屋;它是紅磚砌的,有白色的窗子,有真正的細棉布窗簾、一扇前門和一個煙囪。

passages.original: IT belonged to two Dolls called Lucinda and Jane; at least it belonged to Lucinda, but she never ordered meals.
passages.vernacular: 佢屬於兩個叫露辛達同簡嘅玩偶;至少佢屬於露辛達,不過佢從不點菜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它屬於兩個叫露辛達和簡的玩偶;至少它屬於露辛達,可是她從不點菜。

passages.original: Jane was the Cook; but she never did any cooking, because the dinner had been bought ready-made, in a box full of shavings.
passages.vernacular: 簡係廚子;不過佢從不做飯,因為晚飯係現成買嚟嘅,裝喺一個滿係刨花嘅盒子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡是廚子;可是她從不做飯,因為晚飯是現成買來的,裝在一個滿是刨花的盒子裡。

passages.original: THERE were two red lobsters and a ham, a fish, a pudding, and some pears and oranges.
passages.vernacular: 有兩隻紅龍蝦、一塊火腿、一條魚、一個布丁,仲有啲梨同橘子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有兩隻紅龍蝦、一塊火腿、一條魚、一個布丁,還有一些梨和橘子。

passages.original: They would not come off the plates, but they were extremely beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔能夠從盤子上攞下嚟,但佢哋極其漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不能從盤子上拿下來,但它們極其漂亮。

passages.original: ONE morning Lucinda and Jane had gone out for a drive in the doll's perambulator.
passages.vernacular: 一天早晨,露辛達同簡坐住玩偶嘅嬰兒車出去兜風喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天早晨,露辛達和簡坐著玩偶的嬰兒車出去兜風了。

passages.original: There was no one in the nursery, and it was very quiet.
passages.vernacular: 育兒室裡冇人,好安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 育兒室裡沒有人,非常安靜。

passages.original: Presently there was a little scuffling, scratching noise in a corner near the fire-place, where there was a hole under the skirting-board.
passages.vernacular: 不久,壁爐附近嘅一個角落裡傳嚟一陣小小嘅窸窸窣窣嘅抓撓聲,嗰度嘅踢腳板下有一個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,壁爐附近的一個角落裡傳來一陣小小的窸窸窣窣的抓撓聲,那裡的踢腳板下有一個洞。

passages.original: Tom Thumb put out his head for a moment, and then popped it in again.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指把頭伸出嚟一會兒,然後又縮咗回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指把頭伸出來一會兒,然後又縮了回去。

passages.original: Tom Thumb was a mouse.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指係一隻老鼠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指是一隻老鼠。

passages.original: A MINUTE afterwards, Hunca Munca, his wife, put her head out, too; and when she saw that there was no one in the nursery, she ventured out on the oilcloth under the coal-box.
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘後,佢嘅妻子杭卡·蒙卡都伸出頭嚟;當佢睇見育兒室裡冇人,佢就冒險出嚟,走到煤箱下面嘅油布上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘後,他的妻子杭卡·蒙卡也伸出頭來;當她看見育兒室裡沒有人,她就冒險出來,走到煤箱下面的油布上。

passages.original: THE doll's-house stood at the other side of the fire-place.
passages.vernacular: 玩偶屋立喺壁爐嘅另一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玩偶屋立在壁爐的另一邊。

passages.original: Tom Thumb and Hunca Munca went cautiously across the hearthrug.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指同杭卡·蒙卡小心地走過壁爐前嘅地毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指和杭卡·蒙卡小心地走過壁爐前的地毯。

passages.original: They pushed the front door--it was not fast.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋推咗推前門——冇關緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們推了推前門——沒有關緊。

passages.original: TOM THUMB and Hunca Munca went upstairs and peeped into the dining-room.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指同杭卡·蒙卡走上樓,窺睇餐廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指和杭卡·蒙卡走上樓,窺看餐廳。

passages.original: Then they squeaked with joy!
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋高興得吱吱叫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們高興得吱吱叫!

passages.original: Such a lovely dinner was laid out upon the table!
passages.vernacular: 桌子上擺住幾咁美妙嘅晚餐啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桌子上擺著多麼美妙的晚餐啊!

passages.original: There were tin spoons, and lead knives and forks, and two dolly-chairs--all so convenient!
passages.vernacular: 有錫勺子、鉛刀叉同兩把玩偶椅子——都咁方便!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有錫勺子、鉛刀叉和兩把玩偶椅子——都那麼方便!

passages.original: TOM THUMB set to work at once to carve the ham.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指即刻動手切火腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指立刻動手切火腿。

passages.original: It was a beautiful shiny yellow, streaked with red.
passages.vernacular: 佢係漂亮光亮嘅黃色,帶住紅色條紋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是漂亮光亮的黃色,帶著紅色條紋。

passages.original: The knife crumpled up and hurt him; he put his finger in his mouth.
passages.vernacular: 刀子捲咗起嚟,傷咗佢;佢把手指放進嘴裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刀子捲了起來,傷了他;他把手指放進嘴裡。

passages.original: "It is not boiled enough; it is hard.
passages.vernacular: 「煮得唔夠熟;好硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「煮得不夠熟;很硬。

passages.original: You have a try, Hunca Munca."
passages.vernacular: 你試試,杭卡·蒙卡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你試試,杭卡·蒙卡。」

passages.original: HUNCA MUNCA stood up in her chair, and chopped at the ham with another lead knife.
passages.vernacular: 杭卡·蒙卡站喺佢嘅椅子上,用另一把鉛刀去砍火腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杭卡·蒙卡站在她的椅子上,用另一把鉛刀去砍火腿。

passages.original: "It's as hard as the hams at the cheesemonger's," said Hunca Munca.
passages.vernacular: 「佢同乳酪商店裡嘅火腿一樣硬,」杭卡·蒙卡講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它和乳酪商店裡的火腿一樣硬,」杭卡·蒙卡說。

passages.original: THE ham broke off the plate with a jerk, and rolled under the table.
passages.vernacular: 火腿猛地從盤子上掉下嚟,滾到桌子底下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火腿猛地從盤子上掉下來,滾到桌子底下。

passages.original: "Let it alone," said Tom Thumb; "give me some fish, Hunca Munca!"
passages.vernacular: 「別管佢喇,」湯姆拇指講;「畀我些魚,杭卡·蒙卡!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別管它了,」湯姆拇指說;「給我些魚,杭卡·蒙卡!」

passages.original: HUNCA MUNCA tried every tin spoon in turn; the fish was glued to the dish.
passages.vernacular: 杭卡·蒙卡把每把錫勺子都試咗一遍;魚粘喺盤子上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杭卡·蒙卡把每把錫勺子都試了一遍;魚粘在盤子上了。

passages.original: Then Tom Thumb lost his temper.
passages.vernacular: 於是湯姆拇指發脾氣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是湯姆拇指發脾氣了。

passages.original: He put the ham in the middle of the floor, and hit it with the tongs and with the shovel--bang, bang, smash, smash!
passages.vernacular: 佢把火腿放喺地板中央,用火鉗同鏟子打佢——砰、砰、砸、砸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把火腿放在地板中央,用火鉗和鏟子打它——砰、砰、砸、砸!

passages.original: The ham flew all into pieces, for underneath the shiny paint it was made of nothing but plaster!
passages.vernacular: 火腿炸成咗碎片,因為嗰層亮光漆下面,佢只不過係石膏做嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火腿炸成了碎片,因為那層亮光漆下面,它只不過是石膏做的!

passages.original: THEN there was no end to the rage and disappointment of Tom Thumb and Hunca Munca.
passages.vernacular: 於是湯姆拇指同杭卡·蒙卡嘅憤怒同失望冇完冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是湯姆拇指和杭卡·蒙卡的憤怒和失望沒完沒了。

passages.original: They broke up the pudding, the lobsters, the pears and the oranges.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋砸碎咗布丁、龍蝦、梨同橘子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們砸碎了布丁、龍蝦、梨和橘子。

passages.original: As the fish would not come off the plate, they put it into the red-hot crinkly paper fire in the kitchen; but it would not burn either.
passages.vernacular: 因為魚唔能夠從盤子上攞下嚟,佢哋把佢放進廚房裡紅彤彤嘅皺紙火裡;不過佢都燒不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為魚不能從盤子上拿下來,他們把它放進廚房裡紅彤彤的皺紙火裡;可是它也燒不著。

passages.original: TOM THUMB went up the kitchen chimney and looked out at the top--there was no soot.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指爬上廚房嘅煙囪,從頂上往外睇——冇煤煙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指爬上廚房的煙囪,從頂上往外看——沒有煤煙。

passages.original: WHILE Tom Thumb was up the chimney, Hunca Munca had another disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆拇指喺煙囪裡嘅時候,杭卡·蒙卡又遇到咗一個失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拇指在煙囪裡的時候,杭卡·蒙卡又遇到了一個失望。

passages.original: She found some tiny canisters upon the dresser, labelled--Rice--Coffee--Sago--but when she turned them upside down, there was nothing inside except red and blue beads.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺碗櫥上發現咗啲小罐子,貼住標籤——米——咖啡——西米——不過佢把佢哋倒過嚟,裡面除咗紅色同藍色嘅珠子,乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在碗櫥上發現了一些小罐子,貼著標籤——米——咖啡——西米——可是她把它們倒過來,裡面除了紅色和藍色的珠子,什麼也沒有。

passages.original: THEN those mice set to work to do all the mischief they could--especially Tom Thumb!
passages.vernacular: 於是嗰啲老鼠就動手做佢哋能做嘅一切壞事——特別係湯姆拇指!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是那些老鼠就動手做他們能做的一切壞事——特別是湯姆拇指!

passages.original: He took Jane's clothes out of the chest of drawers in her bedroom, and he threw them out of the top floor window.
passages.vernacular: 佢把簡嘅衣服從佢臥室嘅五斗櫃裡攞出嚟,從頂樓嘅窗子扔咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把簡的衣服從她臥室的五斗櫃裡拿出來,從頂樓的窗子扔了出去。

passages.original: But Hunca Munca had a frugal mind.
passages.vernacular: 不過杭卡·蒙卡好節儉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是杭卡·蒙卡很節儉。

passages.original: After pulling half the feathers out of Lucinda's bolster, she remembered that she herself was in want of a feather bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢把露辛達嘅枕頭扯掉一半羽毛後,想起佢自己都缺一張羽毛床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把露辛達的枕頭扯掉一半羽毛後,想起她自己也缺一張羽毛床。

passages.original: WITH Tom Thumb's assistance she carried the bolster downstairs, and across the hearth-rug.
passages.vernacular: 喺湯姆拇指嘅幫助下,佢把枕頭搬下樓,穿過壁爐前嘅地毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在湯姆拇指的幫助下,她把枕頭搬下樓,穿過壁爐前的地毯。

passages.original: It was difficult to squeeze the bolster into the mouse-hole; but they managed it somehow.
passages.vernacular: 把枕頭擠進老鼠洞好難;但佢哋唔知點算到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把枕頭擠進老鼠洞很難;但他們不知怎麼辦到了。

passages.original: THEN Hunca Munca went back and fetched a chair, a book-case, a bird-cage, and several small odds and ends.
passages.vernacular: 然後杭卡·蒙卡回去攞咗一把椅子、一個書櫃、一個鳥籠同幾樣零碎小嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後杭卡·蒙卡回去拿了一把椅子、一個書櫃、一個鳥籠和幾樣零碎小東西。

passages.original: The book-case and the bird-cage refused to go into the mouse-hole.
passages.vernacular: 書櫃同鳥籠點都進不咗老鼠洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書櫃和鳥籠怎麼也進不了老鼠洞。

passages.original: HUNCA MUNCA left them behind the coal-box, and went to fetch a cradle.
passages.vernacular: 杭卡·蒙卡把佢哋留喺煤箱後面,去攞一張搖籃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杭卡·蒙卡把它們留在煤箱後面,去拿一張搖籃。

passages.original: HUNCA MUNCA was just returning with another chair, when suddenly there was a noise of talking outside upon the landing.
passages.vernacular: 杭卡·蒙卡剛攞住另一把椅子回嚟,突然外面嘅樓梯平台上傳來講話聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杭卡·蒙卡剛拿著另一把椅子回來,突然外面的樓梯平台上傳來說話聲。

passages.original: The mice rushed back to their hole, and the dolls came into the nursery.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠哋衝回洞裡,玩偶哋進咗育兒室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠們衝回洞裡,玩偶們進了育兒室。

passages.original: WHAT a sight met the eyes of Jane and Lucinda!
passages.vernacular: 簡同露辛達睇到嘅係點樣一幅景象啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露辛達看到的是怎樣一幅景象啊!

passages.original: Lucinda sat upon the upset kitchen stove and stared; and Jane leant against the kitchen dresser and smiled--but neither of them made any remark.
passages.vernacular: 露辛達坐喺翻倒嘅廚房爐子上瞪住眼;簡靠喺廚房碗櫥上微笑——不過佢哋邊個都冇講一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露辛達坐在翻倒的廚房爐子上瞪著眼;簡靠在廚房碗櫥上微笑——可是她們誰也沒說一句話。

passages.original: THE book-case and the bird-cage were rescued from under the coal-box--but Hunca Munca has got the cradle, and some of Lucinda's clothes.
passages.vernacular: 書櫃同鳥籠從煤箱下面被救咗出嚟——不過杭卡·蒙卡攞走咗搖籃同露辛達嘅啲衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書櫃和鳥籠從煤箱下面被救了出來——可是杭卡·蒙卡拿走了搖籃和露辛達的一些衣服。

passages.original: SHE also has some useful pots and pans, and several other things.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲攞咗啲有用嘅鍋碗瓢盆同幾樣別嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還拿了一些有用的鍋碗瓢盆和幾樣別的東西。

passages.original: THE little girl that the doll's-house belonged to, said,--"I will get a doll dressed like a policeman!"
passages.vernacular: 玩偶屋所屬嘅小女孩講:「我要找一個打扮成警察嘅玩偶!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玩偶屋所屬的小女孩說:「我要找一個打扮成警察的玩偶!」

passages.original: BUT the nurse said,--"I will set a mouse-trap!"
passages.vernacular: 不過保姆講:「我要放一個捕鼠器!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是保姆說:「我要放一個捕鼠器!」

passages.original: SO that is the story of the two Bad Mice,--but they were not so very very naughty after all, because Tom Thumb paid for everything he broke.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係兩隻壞老鼠嘅故事——不過佢哋到底都冇咁壞,因為湯姆拇指為佢弄壞嘅一切付咗錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是兩隻壞老鼠的故事——可是他們到底也沒有那麼壞,因為湯姆拇指為他弄壞的一切付了錢。

passages.original: He found a crooked sixpence under the hearthrug; and upon Christmas Eve, he and Hunca Munca stuffed it into one of the stockings of Lucinda and Jane.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺壁爐前嘅地毯下發現一枚彎曲嘅六便士;到咗聖誕前夜,佢同杭卡·蒙卡把佢塞進咗露辛達同簡嘅一隻長襪裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在壁爐前的地毯下發現一枚彎曲的六便士;到了聖誕前夜,他和杭卡·蒙卡把它塞進了露辛達和簡的一隻長襪裡。

passages.original: AND very early every morning--before anybody is awake--Hunca Munca comes with her dust-pan and her broom to sweep the Dollies' house!
passages.vernacular: 每天一大清早——喺大家都醒嚟之前——杭卡·蒙卡就攞住佢嘅簸箕同掃帚嚟打掃玩偶哋嘅屋子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天一大清早——在大家都醒來之前——杭卡·蒙卡就拿著她的簸箕和掃帚來打掃玩偶們的屋子!

chapters.title: The Tale of Tom Kitten 湯姆小貓的故事

passages.original: CH Once upon a time there were three little kittens, and their names were Mittens, Tom Kitten, and Moppet.
passages.vernacular: 從前有三隻小貓,佢哋嘅名字叫米滕斯、湯姆小貓同莫佩特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有三隻小貓,它們的名字叫米滕斯、湯姆小貓和莫佩特。

passages.original: They had dear little fur coats of their own; and they tumbled about the doorstep and played in the dust.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋有自己可愛嘅小毛皮外套;佢哋喺門階上翻滾,喺塵土裡玩耍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們有自己可愛的小毛皮外套;它們在門階上翻滾,在塵土裡玩耍。

passages.original: But one day their mother--Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit--expected friends to tea; so she fetched the kittens indoors, to wash and dress them, before the fine company arrived.
passages.vernacular: 不過有一天,佢哋嘅媽媽——塔比莎·特威奇特太太——要請朋友嚟飲茶;所以佢把小貓哋叫進屋裡,畀佢哋洗澡、穿衣服,趕喺貴客到來之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是有一天,它們的媽媽——塔比莎·特威奇特太太——要請朋友來喝茶;所以她把小貓們叫進屋裡,給它們洗澡、穿衣服,趕在貴客到來之前。

passages.original: First she scrubbed their faces (this one is Moppet).
passages.vernacular: 佢先擦洗佢哋嘅臉(呢一隻係莫佩特)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她先擦洗它們的臉(這一隻是莫佩特)。

passages.original: Then she brushed their fur, (this one is Mittens).
passages.vernacular: 然後佢梳理佢哋嘅毛(呢一隻係米滕斯)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她梳理它們的毛(這一隻是米滕斯)。

passages.original: Then she combed their tails and whiskers (this is Tom Kitten).
passages.vernacular: 然後佢梳佢哋嘅尾巴同鬍鬚(呢一隻係湯姆小貓)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她梳它們的尾巴和鬍鬚(這一隻是湯姆小貓)。

passages.original: Tom was very naughty, and he scratched.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆好淘氣,佢仲抓人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆很淘氣,他還抓人。

passages.original: Mrs. Tabitha dressed Moppet and Mittens in clean pinafores and tuckers; and then she took all sorts of elegant uncomfortable clothes out of a chest of drawers, in order to dress up her son Thomas.
passages.vernacular: 塔比莎太太畀莫佩特同米滕斯穿上乾淨嘅圍裙同胸飾;然後佢從一個五斗櫃裡攞出各種優雅卻不舒服嘅衣服,畀佢兒子托馬斯穿戴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔比莎太太給莫佩特和米滕斯穿上乾淨的圍裙和胸飾;然後她從一個五斗櫃裡拿出各種優雅卻不舒服的衣服,給她兒子托馬斯穿戴。

passages.original: Tom Kitten was very fat, and he had grown; several buttons burst off.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆小貓好胖,而且長大喇;好幾顆鈕扣崩掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆小貓很胖,而且長大了;好幾顆鈕扣崩掉了。

passages.original: His mother sewed them on again.
passages.vernacular: 佢母親又把佢哋縫上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他母親又把它們縫上了。

passages.original: When the three kittens were ready, Mrs. Tabitha unwisely turned them out into the garden, to be out of the way while she made hot buttered toast.
passages.vernacular: 三隻小貓都準備好喇,塔比莎太太不明智地把佢哋趕到花園裡,免得妨礙佢做熱奶油吐司。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三隻小貓都準備好了,塔比莎太太不明智地把它們趕到花園裡,免得妨礙她做熱奶油吐司。

passages.original: "Now keep your frocks clean, children!
passages.vernacular: 「而家,細路哋,保持你哋嘅衣服乾淨!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,孩子們,保持你們的衣服乾淨!

passages.original: You must walk on your hind legs.
passages.vernacular: 你哋必須用後腿走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們必須用後腿走路。

passages.original: Keep away from the dirty ash-pit, and from Sally Henny Penny, and from the pig-stye and the Puddle-Ducks."
passages.vernacular: 離髒灰坑遠點,離母雞莎莉·亨尼·彭尼遠點,離豬圈同鴨子遠點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離髒灰坑遠點,離母雞莎莉·亨尼·彭尼遠點,離豬圈和鴨子遠點。」

passages.original: Moppet and Mittens walked down the garden path unsteadily.
passages.vernacular: 莫佩特同米滕斯搖搖晃晃地沿住花園小路走下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莫佩特和米滕斯搖搖晃晃地沿著花園小路走下去。

passages.original: Presently they trod upon their pinafores and fell on their noses.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,佢哋踩到咗自己嘅圍裙,摔咗個鼻子住地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,它們踩到了自己的圍裙,摔了個鼻子著地。

passages.original: When they stood up there were several green smears!
passages.vernacular: 佢哋站起嚟嘅時候,身上有好幾處綠色嘅汙跡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們站起來的時候,身上有好幾處綠色的汙跡!

passages.original: "Let us climb up the rockery, and sit on the garden wall," said Moppet.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋爬上假山,坐喺花園嘅牆頭吧,」莫佩特講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們爬上假山,坐在花園的牆頭吧,」莫佩特說。

passages.original: They turned their pinafores back to front, and went up with a skip and a jump; Moppet's white tucker fell down into the road.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把圍裙前後轉過嚟,蹦蹦跳跳地爬咗上去;莫佩特嘅白胸飾掉到咗路上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們把圍裙前後轉過來,蹦蹦跳跳地爬了上去;莫佩特的白胸飾掉到了路上。

passages.original: Tom Kitten was quite unable to jump when walking upon his hind legs in trousers.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆小貓穿住褲子用後腿走路,完全跳不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆小貓穿著褲子用後腿走路,完全跳不起來。

passages.original: He came up the rockery by degrees, breaking the ferns, and shedding buttons right and left.
passages.vernacular: 佢啲啲地爬上假山,弄斷咗蕨類,左右兩邊都喺掉鈕扣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一點一點地爬上假山,弄斷了蕨類,左右兩邊都在掉鈕扣。

passages.original: He was all in pieces when he reached the top of the wall.
passages.vernacular: 佢爬到牆頭時渾身都散咗架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他爬到牆頭時渾身都散了架。

passages.original: Moppet and Mittens tried to pull him together; his hat fell off, and the rest of his buttons burst.
passages.vernacular: 莫佩特同米滕斯試住把佢拉攏喺一起;佢嘅帽子掉喇,剩下嘅鈕扣都崩開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莫佩特和米滕斯試著把他拉攏在一起;他的帽子掉了,剩下的鈕扣也崩開了。

passages.original: While they were in difficulties, there was a pit pat paddle pat! and the three Puddle-Ducks came along the hard high road, marching one behind the other and doing the goose step--pit pat paddle pat! pit pat waddle pat!
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正陷入困境時,傳嚟啪嗒啪嗒啪嗒啪!三隻鴨子沿住堅硬嘅大路走嚟,一隻接一隻,邁住鵝步——啪嗒啪嗒啪嗒啪!啪嗒啪嗒搖啪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們正陷入困境時,傳來啪嗒啪嗒啪嗒啪!三隻鴨子沿著堅硬的大路走來,一隻接一隻,邁著鵝步——啪嗒啪嗒啪嗒啪!啪嗒啪嗒搖啪!

passages.original: They stopped and stood in a row, and stared up at the kittens.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋停下嚟,排成一排站住,抬頭望住小貓哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們停下來,排成一排站著,抬頭望著小貓們。

passages.original: They had very small eyes and looked surprised.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅眼睛好小,顯得驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們的眼睛很小,顯得驚訝。

passages.original: Then the two duck-birds, Rebeccah and Jemima Puddle-Duck, picked up the hat and tucker and put them on.
passages.vernacular: 然後兩隻母鴨,麗貝卡同傑瑪·水坑鴨,撿起帽子同胸飾,穿戴咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後兩隻母鴨,麗貝卡和傑瑪·水坑鴨,撿起帽子和胸飾,穿戴了起來。

passages.original: Mittens laughed so that she fell off the wall.
passages.vernacular: 米滕斯笑得從牆上掉咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米滕斯笑得從牆上掉了下去。

passages.original: Moppet and Tom descended after her; the pinafores and all the rest of Tom's clothes came off on the way down.
passages.vernacular: 莫佩特同湯姆跟住佢爬下去;圍裙同湯姆其餘嘅衣服喺下嚟嘅路上都掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莫佩特和湯姆跟著她爬下去;圍裙和湯姆其餘的衣服在下來的路上都掉了。

passages.original: "Come!
Mr. Drake Puddle-Duck," said Moppet--"Come and help us to dress him!
passages.vernacular: 水坑鴨先生,」莫佩特講——「嚟幫我哋畀佢穿衣服!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水坑鴨先生,」莫佩特說——「來幫我們給他穿衣服!

passages.original: Come and button up Tom!"
passages.vernacular: 嚟畀湯姆扣上扣子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來給湯姆扣上扣子!」

passages.original: Mr. Drake Puddle-Duck advanced in a slow sideways manner, and picked up the various articles.
passages.vernacular: 水坑鴨先生慢慢地側住身走上嚟,撿起各件衣物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水坑鴨先生慢慢地側著身走上來,撿起各件衣物。

passages.original: But he put them on himself!
passages.vernacular: 不過佢自己穿上喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是他自己穿上了!

passages.original: They fitted him even worse than Tom Kitten.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋穿喺佢身上比穿喺湯姆小貓身上更不合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們穿在他身上比穿在湯姆小貓身上更不合適。

passages.original: "It's a very fine morning!" said Mr. Drake Puddle-Duck.
passages.vernacular: 「今日早晨天氣真好!」水坑鴨先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早晨天氣真好!」水坑鴨先生說。

passages.original: And he and Jemima and Rebeccah Puddle-Duck set off up the road, keeping step--pit pat, paddle pat! pit pat, waddle pat!
passages.vernacular: 佢同傑瑪同麗貝卡·水坑鴨沿住路走喇,步伐一致——啪嗒啪嗒,啪嗒搖啪!啪嗒啪嗒,搖啪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他同傑瑪和麗貝卡·水坑鴨沿著路走了,步伐一致——啪嗒啪嗒,啪嗒搖啪!啪嗒啪嗒,搖啪!

passages.original: Then Tabitha Twitchit came down the garden and found her kittens on the wall with no clothes on.
passages.vernacular: 然後塔比莎·特威奇特走下花園,發現佢嘅小貓哋喺牆上冇穿衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後塔比莎·特威奇特走下花園,發現她的小貓們在牆上沒穿衣服。

passages.original: She pulled them off the wall, smacked them, and took them back to the house.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢哋從牆上拉下嚟,打咗佢哋,帶佢哋回屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它們從牆上拉下來,打了它們,帶它們回屋。

passages.original: "My friends will arrive in a minute, and you are not fit to be seen; I am affronted," said Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅朋友哋一分鐘後就到,你哋而家見唔得人;我太丟臉喇,」塔比莎·特威奇特太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的朋友們一分鐘後就到,你們現在見不得人;我太丟臉了,」塔比莎·特威奇特太太說。

passages.original: She sent them upstairs; and I am sorry to say she told her friends that they were in bed with the measles; which was not true.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢哋送上樓;我好遺憾地講,佢告訴朋友哋佢哋得咗麻疹躺喺床上;呢唔係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它們送上樓;我很遺憾地說,她告訴朋友們它們得了麻疹躺在床上;這不是真的。

passages.original: Quite the contrary; they were not in bed: not in the least.
passages.vernacular: 恰恰相反;佢哋冇躺喺床上:啲兒都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恰恰相反;它們沒有躺在床上:一點兒也沒有。

passages.original: Somehow there were very extraordinary noises over-head, which disturbed the dignity and repose of the tea party.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,頭頂上傳嚟好奇怪嘅聲音,擾亂咗茶會嘅莊重同寧靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,頭頂上傳來非常奇怪的聲音,擾亂了茶會的莊重和寧靜。

passages.original: And I think that some day I shall have to make another, larger, book, to tell you more about Tom Kitten!
passages.vernacular: 我想總有一天,我得再做一本更大嘅書,告訴你哋更多關於湯姆小貓嘅事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想總有一天,我得再做一本更大的書,告訴你們更多關於湯姆小貓的事!

passages.original: As for the Puddle-Ducks--they went into a pond.
passages.vernacular: 至於水坑鴨哋——佢哋走進咗一個池塘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於水坑鴨們——它們走進了一個池塘。

passages.original: The clothes all came off directly, because there were no buttons.
passages.vernacular: 衣服即刻都掉喇,因為冇鈕扣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 衣服馬上都掉了,因為沒有鈕扣。

passages.original: And Mr. Drake Puddle-Duck, and Jemima and Rebeccah, have been looking for them ever since.
passages.vernacular: 而水坑鴨先生同傑瑪、麗貝卡,從嗰以後一直喺找佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而水坑鴨先生和傑瑪、麗貝卡,從那以後一直在找它們。

chapters.title: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck 傑瑪·水坑鴨的故事

passages.original: CH What a funny sight it is to see a brood of ducklings with a hen!
passages.vernacular: 睇到一隻母雞帶住一群小鴨子,幾咁有趣嘅景象啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到一隻母雞帶著一群小鴨子,多麼有趣的景象啊!

passages.original: --Listen to the story of Jemima Puddle-duck, who was annoyed because the farmer's wife would not let her hatch her own eggs.
passages.vernacular: ——聽聽傑瑪·水坑鴨嘅故事,佢好惱火,因為農夫嘅妻子不讓佢孵自己嘅蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: ——聽聽傑瑪·水坑鴨的故事,她很惱火,因為農夫的妻子不讓她孵自己的蛋。

passages.original: Her sister-in-law, Mrs. Rebeccah Puddle-duck, was perfectly willing to leave the hatching to some one else--"I have not the patience to sit on a nest for twenty-eight days; and no more have you, Jemima.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅嫂子麗貝卡·水坑鴨太太完全願意把孵蛋嘅事交畀別人——「我冇耐心喺窩裡坐二十八天;你都冇,傑瑪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的嫂子麗貝卡·水坑鴨太太完全願意把孵蛋的事交給別人——「我沒有耐心在窩裡坐二十八天;你也沒有,傑瑪。

passages.original: You would let them go cold; you know you would!"
passages.vernacular: 你會讓佢哋變冷嘅;你知道你會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會讓它們變冷的;你知道你會!」

passages.original: "I wish to hatch my own eggs; I will hatch them all by myself," quacked Jemima Puddle-duck.
passages.vernacular: 「我想孵我自己嘅蛋;我要自己把佢哋全部孵出嚟,」傑瑪·水坑鴨嘎嘎地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想孵我自己的蛋;我要自己把它們全部孵出來,」傑瑪·水坑鴨嘎嘎地說。

passages.original: She tried to hide her eggs; but they were always found and carried off.
passages.vernacular: 佢試住藏佢嘅蛋;不過佢哋總是被找到並攞走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她試著藏她的蛋;可是它們總是被找到並拿走。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck became quite desperate.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨變得好絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨變得十分絕望。

passages.original: She determined to make a nest right away from the farm.
passages.vernacular: 佢決心喺遠離農場嘅地方做一個窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她決心在遠離農場的地方做一個窩。

passages.original: She set off on a fine spring afternoon along the cart-road that leads over the hill.
passages.vernacular: 一個晴朗嘅春天下午,佢沿住通過山丘嘅車道出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個晴朗的春天下午,她沿著通過山丘的車道出發了。

passages.original: She was wearing a shawl and a poke bonnet.
passages.vernacular: 佢戴住披肩同一頂寬邊帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她戴著披肩和一頂寬邊帽。

passages.original: When she reached the top of the hill, she saw a wood in the distance.
passages.vernacular: 佢到達山頂時,睇見遠處有一片樹林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她到達山頂時,看見遠處有一片樹林。

passages.original: She thought that it looked a safe quiet spot.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得佢睇起嚟係個安全安靜嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她覺得它看起來是個安全安靜的地方。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck was not much in the habit of flying.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨不太習慣飛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨不太習慣飛。

passages.original: She ran downhill a few yards flapping her shawl, and then she jumped off into the air.
passages.vernacular: 佢揮動住披肩跑下山幾碼,然後跳到空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她揮動著披肩跑下山幾碼,然後跳到空中。

passages.original: She flew beautifully when she had got a good start.
passages.vernacular: 有咗好嘅起步,佢飛得好漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有了好的起步,她飛得很漂亮。

passages.original: She skimmed along over the tree-tops until she saw an open place in the middle of the wood, where the trees and brushwood had been cleared.
passages.vernacular: 佢掠過樹梢,直到睇到樹林中央一塊空地,嗰度嘅樹木同灌木已被清除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她掠過樹梢,直到看到樹林中央一塊空地,那裡的樹木和灌木已被清除。

passages.original: Jemima alighted rather heavily, and began to waddle about in search of a convenient dry nesting-place.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪相當重地降落喇,開始搖搖擺擺地走動,尋找一個方便嘅乾燥築巢地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪相當重地降落了,開始搖搖擺擺地走動,尋找一個方便的乾燥築巢地。

passages.original: She rather fancied a tree-stump amongst some tall fox-gloves.
passages.vernacular: 佢挺鍾意一棵喺高大毛地黃中間嘅樹樁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她挺喜歡一棵在高大毛地黃中間的樹樁。

passages.original: But--seated upon the stump, she was startled to find an elegantly dressed gentleman reading a newspaper.
passages.vernacular: 不過——坐喺嗰樹樁上嘅,係一位衣住優雅嘅先生,正在睇報紙,呢讓佢食咗一驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是——坐在那樹樁上的,是一位衣著優雅的先生,正在看報紙,這讓她吃了一驚。

passages.original: He had black prick ears and sandy coloured whiskers.
passages.vernacular: 佢有黑色嘅尖耳朵同沙色嘅鬍鬚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有黑色的尖耳朵和沙色的鬍鬚。

passages.original: "Quack?" said Jemima Puddle-duck, with her head and her bonnet on one side--"Quack?"
passages.vernacular: 「嘎?」傑瑪·水坑鴨講,頭同帽子歪向一邊——「嘎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嘎?」傑瑪·水坑鴨說,頭和帽子歪向一邊——「嘎?」

passages.original: The gentleman raised his eyes above his newspaper and looked curiously at Jemima--
passages.vernacular: 嗰位先生從報紙上方抬起眼睛,好奇地睇住傑瑪——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位先生從報紙上方抬起眼睛,好奇地看著傑瑪——

passages.original: "Madam, have you lost your way?" said he.
passages.vernacular: 「太太,您迷路咗嗎?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太太,您迷路了嗎?」他說。

passages.original: He had a long bushy tail which he was sitting upon, as the stump was somewhat damp.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一條又長又蓬鬆嘅尾巴,佢坐喺上面,因為樹樁有點潮濕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一條又長又蓬鬆的尾巴,他坐在上面,因為樹樁有點潮濕。

passages.original: Jemima thought him mighty civil and handsome.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪覺得佢好有禮貌,而且英俊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪覺得他非常有禮貌,而且英俊。

passages.original: She explained that she had not lost her way, but that she was trying to find a convenient dry nesting-place.
passages.vernacular: 佢解釋講佢冇迷路,只係想找一個方便嘅乾燥築巢地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她解釋說她沒有迷路,只是想找一個方便的乾燥築巢地。

passages.original: "Ah! is that so? indeed!" said the gentleman with sandy whiskers, looking curiously at Jemima.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!係咁樣嗎?真嘅!」長住沙色鬍鬚嘅先生講,好奇地睇住傑瑪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!是這樣嗎?真的!」長著沙色鬍鬚的先生說,好奇地看著傑瑪。

passages.original: He folded up the newspaper, and put it in his coat-tail pocket.
passages.vernacular: 佢把報紙折起嚟,放進佢嘅外套後兜裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把報紙折起來,放進他的外套後兜裡。

passages.original: Jemima complained of the superfluous hen.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪抱怨嗰多餘嘅母雞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪抱怨那多餘的母雞。

passages.original: "Indeed! how interesting!
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!多有意思!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!多有意思!

passages.original: I wish I could meet with that fowl.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望能遇到嗰隻雞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望能遇到那隻雞。

passages.original: I would teach it to mind its own business!"
passages.vernacular: 我會教佢管好自己嘅事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會教它管好自己的事!」

passages.original: "But as to a nest--there is no difficulty: I have a sackful of feathers in my wood-shed.
passages.vernacular: 「至於窩——冇困難:我嘅柴棚裡有一袋子羽毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「至於窩——沒有困難:我的柴棚裡有一袋子羽毛。

passages.original: No, my dear madam, you will be in nobody's way.
passages.vernacular: 不,親愛嘅太太,您唔會妨礙任何人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,親愛的太太,您不會妨礙任何人。

passages.original: You may sit there as long as you like," said the bushy long-tailed gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 您愛坐多久就坐多久,」嗰位蓬鬆長尾巴嘅先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您愛坐多久就坐多久,」那位蓬鬆長尾巴的先生說。

passages.original: He led the way to a very retired, dismal-looking house amongst the fox-gloves.
passages.vernacular: 佢領路走向毛地黃中間一間好僻靜、睇起嚟陰暗嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他領路走向毛地黃中間一間非常僻靜、看起來陰暗的房子。

passages.original: It was built of faggots and turf, and there were two broken pails, one on top of another, by way of a chimney.
passages.vernacular: 佢係用柴捆同草皮建嘅,有兩個破桶,一個疊喺另一個上面,當作煙囪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是用柴捆和草皮建的,有兩個破桶,一個疊在另一個上面,當作煙囪。

passages.original: "This is my summer residence; you would not find my earth--my winter house--so convenient," said the hospitable gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我嘅夏季住所;您會發現我嘅地洞——我嘅冬季住宅——冇咁方便,」好客嘅先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我的夏季住所;您會發現我的地洞——我的冬季住宅——沒有這麼方便,」好客的先生說。

passages.original: There was a tumble-down shed at the back of the house, made of old soap-boxes.
passages.vernacular: 房子後面有一個搖搖欲墜嘅棚子,係用舊肥皂箱做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子後面有一個搖搖欲墜的棚子,是用舊肥皂箱做的。

passages.original: The gentleman opened the door, and showed Jemima in.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位先生打開門,帶傑瑪進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位先生打開門,帶傑瑪進去。

passages.original: The shed was almost quite full of feathers--it was almost suffocating; but it was comfortable and very soft.
passages.vernacular: 棚子裡幾乎裝滿咗羽毛——幾乎讓人窒息;但佢好舒服都好柔軟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 棚子裡幾乎裝滿了羽毛——幾乎讓人窒息;但它很舒服也很柔軟。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck was rather surprised to find such a vast quantity of feathers.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨好驚訝,竟發現有咁大量嘅羽毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨很驚訝,竟發現有這麼大量的羽毛。

passages.original: But it was very comfortable; and she made a nest without any trouble at all.
passages.vernacular: 但係佢好舒服;佢毫不費力地做咗一個窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是它很舒服;她毫不費力地做了一個窩。

passages.original: When she came out, the sandy whiskered gentleman was sitting on a log reading the newspaper--at least he had it spread out, but he was looking over the top of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢出嚟時,沙色鬍鬚嘅先生正坐喺一根圓木上睇報紙——至少佢把佢攤開喇,但佢係從上面窺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她出來時,沙色鬍鬚的先生正坐在一根圓木上看報紙——至少他把它攤開了,但他是從上面窺看。

passages.original: He was so polite, that he seemed almost sorry to let Jemima go home for the night.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁有禮貌,幾乎好像好遺憾讓傑瑪夜裡回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他那麼有禮貌,幾乎好像很遺憾讓傑瑪夜裡回家。

passages.original: He promised to take great care of her nest until she came back again next day.
passages.vernacular: 佢答應喺佢第二天回嚟之前,會好好照睇佢嘅窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他答應在她第二天回來之前,會好好照看她的窩。

passages.original: He said he loved eggs and ducklings; he should be proud to see a fine nestful in his wood-shed.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢愛蛋同小鴨;佢好樂意喺佢嘅柴棚裡睇到一窩漂亮嘅小鴨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他愛蛋和小鴨;他很樂意在他的柴棚裡看到一窩漂亮的小鴨。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck came every afternoon; she laid nine eggs in the nest.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨每天下午都嚟;佢喺窩裡下咗九顆蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨每天下午都來;她在窩裡下了九顆蛋。

passages.original: They were greeny white and very large.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係青白色嘅,好大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們是青白色的,非常大。

passages.original: The foxy gentleman admired them immensely.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位像狐狸似嘅先生極其欣賞佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位像狐狸似的先生極其欣賞它們。

passages.original: He used to turn them over and count them when Jemima was not there.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪不喺時,佢常把佢哋翻過嚟數一數。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪不在時,他常把它們翻過來數一數。

passages.original: At last Jemima told him that she intended to begin to sit next day--"and I will bring a bag of corn with me, so that I need never leave my nest until the eggs are hatched.
passages.vernacular: 最後傑瑪告訴佢,佢打算第二天開始孵——「我會帶一袋玉米嚟,咁樣喺蛋孵出嚟之前我就唔使離開我嘅窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後傑瑪告訴他,她打算第二天開始孵——「我會帶一袋玉米來,這樣在蛋孵出來之前我就不用離開我的窩。

passages.original: They might catch cold," said the conscientious Jemima.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋可能會住涼,」盡責嘅傑瑪講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們可能會著涼,」盡責的傑瑪說。

passages.original: "Madam, I beg you not to trouble yourself with a bag; I will provide oats.
passages.vernacular: 「太太,我請您唔使費心帶袋子;我嚟提供燕麥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太太,我請您不必費心帶袋子;我來提供燕麥。

passages.original: But before you commence your tedious sitting, I intend to give you a treat.
passages.vernacular: 不過喺您開始嗰乏味嘅孵蛋之前,我打算請您享用一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過在您開始那乏味的孵蛋之前,我打算請您享用一頓。

passages.original: Let us have a dinner-party all to ourselves!
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋自己開個晚宴吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們自己開個晚宴吧!

passages.original: "May I ask you to bring up some herbs from the farm-garden to make a savoury omelette?
passages.vernacular: 「我可以請您從農場嘅園子裡帶些香草嚟,做一份美味嘅煎蛋捲嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以請您從農場的園子裡帶些香草來,做一份美味的煎蛋捲嗎?

passages.original: Sage and thyme, and mint and two onions, and some parsley.
passages.vernacular: 鼠尾草、百里香、薄荷同兩個洋蔥,仲有啲香芹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鼠尾草、百里香、薄荷和兩個洋蔥,還有一些香芹。

passages.original: I will provide lard for the stuff--lard for the omelette," said the hospitable gentleman with sandy whiskers.
passages.vernacular: 我嚟提供餡料用嘅豬油——煎蛋捲用嘅豬油,」好客嘅沙色鬍鬚先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來提供餡料用的豬油——煎蛋捲用的豬油,」好客的沙色鬍鬚先生說。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck was a simpleton: not even the mention of sage and onions made her suspicious.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨係個傻瓜:連提到鼠尾草同洋蔥都冇讓佢起疑心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨是個傻瓜:連提到鼠尾草和洋蔥也沒讓她起疑心。

passages.original: She went round the farm-garden, nibbling off snippets of all the different sorts of herbs that are used for stuffing roast duck.
passages.vernacular: 佢繞住農場嘅園子,啄下各種用嚟畀烤鴨做餡嘅香草嘅小段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她繞著農場的園子,啄下各種用來給烤鴨做餡的香草的小段。

passages.original: And she waddled into the kitchen, and got two onions out of a basket.
passages.vernacular: 佢搖搖擺擺走進廚房,從籃子裡攞咗兩個洋蔥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她搖搖擺擺走進廚房,從籃子裡拿了兩個洋蔥。

passages.original: The collie-dog Kep met her coming out, "What are you doing with those onions?
passages.vernacular: 牧羊犬凱普喺佢出嚟時遇見咗佢:「你攞嗰啲洋蔥幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧羊犬凱普在她出來時遇見了她:「你拿那些洋蔥幹什麼?

passages.original: Where do you go every afternoon by yourself, Jemima Puddle-duck?"
passages.vernacular: 你每天下午獨自去邊度,傑瑪·水坑鴨?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你每天下午獨自去哪裡,傑瑪·水坑鴨?」

passages.original: Jemima was rather in awe of the collie; she told him the whole story.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪有點怕嗰條牧羊犬;佢把整個故事都告訴咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪有點怕那條牧羊犬;她把整個故事都告訴了他。

passages.original: The collie listened, with his wise head on one side; he grinned when she described the polite gentleman with sandy whiskers.
passages.vernacular: 牧羊犬歪住佢聰明嘅腦袋聽住;當佢描述嗰位有禮貌嘅沙色鬍鬚先生時,佢咧嘴笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧羊犬歪著他聰明的腦袋聽著;當她描述那位有禮貌的沙色鬍鬚先生時,他咧嘴笑了。

passages.original: He asked several questions about the wood, and about the exact position of the house and shed.
passages.vernacular: 佢問咗幾個關於樹林嘅問題,以及房子同棚子的確切位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他問了幾個關於樹林的問題,以及房子和棚子的確切位置。

passages.original: Then he went out, and trotted down the village.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢出去,小跑住下咗村子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他出去,小跑著下了村子。

passages.original: He went to look for two fox-hound puppies who were out at walk with the butcher.
passages.vernacular: 佢去找兩隻同屠夫一起出嚟散步嘅小獵狐犬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他去找兩隻和屠夫一起出來散步的小獵狐犬。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck went up the cart-road for the last time, on a sunny afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨喺一個陽光燦爛嘅下午最後一次沿住車道走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨在一個陽光燦爛的下午最後一次沿著車道走。

passages.original: She was rather burdened with bunches of herbs and two onions in a bag.
passages.vernacular: 佢背住成束嘅香草同一袋兩個洋蔥,相當食力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她背著成束的香草和一袋兩個洋蔥,相當吃力。

passages.original: She flew over the wood, and alighted opposite the house of the bushy long-tailed gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 佢飛越樹林,降落喺嗰位蓬鬆長尾巴先生嘅房子對面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她飛越樹林,降落在那位蓬鬆長尾巴先生的房子對面。

passages.original: He was sitting on a log; he sniffed the air, and kept glancing uneasily round the wood.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺一根圓木上;佢嗅住空氣,不安地一直四下張望樹林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐在一根圓木上;他嗅著空氣,不安地一直四下張望樹林。

passages.original: When Jemima alighted he quite jumped.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪降落時,佢嚇咗一跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪降落時,他嚇了一跳。

passages.original: "Come into the house as soon as you have looked at your eggs.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇過你嘅蛋就即刻進屋嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看過你的蛋就馬上進屋來。

passages.original: Give me the herbs for the omelette.
passages.vernacular: 把做煎蛋捲嘅香草畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把做煎蛋捲的香草給我。

passages.original: Be sharp!"
passages.vernacular: 快點!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快點!」

passages.original: He was rather abrupt.
passages.vernacular: 佢相當粗暴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他相當粗暴。
