passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck had never heard him speak like that.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨從冇聽過佢嗰樣講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨從沒聽過他那樣說話。

passages.original: She felt surprised, and uncomfortable.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得驚訝,又不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她覺得驚訝,又不舒服。

passages.original: While she was inside she heard pattering feet round the back of the shed.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺裡面時,聽見棚子後面有腳步聲噠噠響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在裡面時,聽見棚子後面有腳步聲噠噠響。

passages.original: Some one with a black nose sniffed at the bottom of the door, and then locked it.
passages.vernacular: 有個黑鼻子嘅人喺門底下嗅咗嗅,然後把門鎖上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個黑鼻子的人在門底下嗅了嗅,然後把門鎖上了。

passages.original: Jemima became much alarmed.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪變得好驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪變得非常驚慌。

passages.original: A moment afterwards there were most awful noises--barking, baying, growls and howls, squealing and groans.
passages.vernacular: 一會兒後傳嚟咗最可怕嘅聲音——吠叫聲、嚎叫聲、咆哮聲同哀號聲、尖叫聲同呻吟聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一會兒後傳來了最可怕的聲音——吠叫聲、嚎叫聲、咆哮聲和哀號聲、尖叫聲和呻吟聲。

passages.original: And nothing more was ever seen of that foxy-whiskered gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 而嗰位長住狐狸鬍鬚嘅先生,再都冇人見過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而那位長著狐狸鬍鬚的先生,再也沒有人見過。

passages.original: Presently Kep opened the door of the shed, and let out Jemima Puddle-duck.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒凱普打開棚子嘅門,放出咗傑瑪·水坑鴨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒凱普打開棚子的門,放出了傑瑪·水坑鴨。

passages.original: Unfortunately the puppies rushed in and gobbled up all the eggs before he could stop them.
passages.vernacular: 不幸嘅係,小狗哋衝進去,喺佢阻止佢哋之前,把所有嘅蛋都吞掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不幸的是,小狗們衝進去,在他阻止它們之前,把所有的蛋都吞掉了。

passages.original: He had a bite on his ear and both the puppies were limping.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅耳朵被咬傷喇,兩隻小狗都一瘸一拐嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的耳朵被咬傷了,兩隻小狗都一瘸一拐的。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck was escorted home in tears on account of those eggs.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨為了嗰啲蛋,流住眼淚被護送回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨為了那些蛋,流著眼淚被護送回家。

passages.original: She laid some more in June, and she was permitted to keep them herself: but only four of them hatched.
passages.vernacular: 佢六月又下咗啲蛋,呢次允許佢自己留住佢哋:不過只孵出咗四隻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她六月又下了一些蛋,這次允許她自己留著它們:可是只孵出了四隻。

passages.original: Jemima Puddle-duck said that it was because of her nerves; but she had always been a bad sitter.
passages.vernacular: 傑瑪·水坑鴨講呢個係因為佢神經不好;不過佢一向係個糟糕嘅孵蛋者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑瑪·水坑鴨說這是因為她神經不好;可是她一向是個糟糕的孵蛋者。

chapters.title: The Tale of Mr. Jeremy Fisher 傑里米·費舍先生的故事

passages.original: CH Once upon a time there was a frog called Mr. Jeremy Fisher; he lived in a little damp house amongst the buttercups at the edge of a pond.
passages.vernacular: 從前有一隻青蛙叫傑里米·費舍先生;佢住喺池塘邊毛茛花叢中一間小小嘅潮濕房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有一隻青蛙叫傑里米·費舍先生;他住在池塘邊毛茛花叢中一間小小的潮濕房子裡。

passages.original: The water was all slippy-sloppy in the larder and in the back passage.
passages.vernacular: 食品儲藏室同後走廊裡全係水,濕漉漉嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 食品儲藏室和後走廊裡全是水,濕漉漉的。

passages.original: But Mr. Jeremy liked getting his feet wet; nobody ever scolded him, and he never caught a cold!
passages.vernacular: 不過傑里米先生鍾意把腳弄濕;從冇人責罵過佢,佢都從不感冒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是傑里米先生喜歡把腳弄濕;從沒有人責罵過他,他也從不感冒!

passages.original: He was quite pleased when he looked out and saw large drops of rain, splashing in the pond--
passages.vernacular: 佢往外睇,睇見大雨點喺池塘裡濺起水花,好高興——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他往外看,看見大雨點在池塘裡濺起水花,非常高興——

passages.original: "I will get some worms and go fishing and catch a dish of minnows for my dinner," said Mr. Jeremy Fisher. "If I catch more than five fish, I will invite my friends Mr. Alderman Ptolemy Tortoise and Sir Isaac Newton.
passages.vernacular: 「我要攞些蚯蚓去釣魚,釣一盤小魚當晚飯,」傑里米·費舍先生講。「如果我釣到五條以上,我就請我嘅朋友托勒密·烏龜市議員同艾薩克·牛頓爵士嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要拿些蚯蚓去釣魚,釣一盤小魚當晚飯,」傑里米·費舍先生說。「如果我釣到五條以上,我就請我的朋友托勒密·烏龜市議員和艾薩克·牛頓爵士來。

passages.original: The Alderman, however, eats salad."
passages.vernacular: 不過市議員只食沙拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過市議員只吃沙拉。」

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy put on a macintosh, and a pair of shiny goloshes; he took his rod and basket, and set off with enormous hops to the place where he kept his boat.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生穿上一件雨衣同一雙發亮嘅膠套鞋;佢攞住釣竿同籃子,邁住巨大嘅跳躍出發,去佢放船嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生穿上一件雨衣和一雙發亮的膠套鞋;他拿著釣竿和籃子,邁著巨大的跳躍出發,去他放船的地方。

passages.original: The boat was round and green, and very like the other lily-leaves.
passages.vernacular: 嗰條船係圓嘅,綠色嘅,好像別嘅瞓蓮葉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那條船是圓的,綠色的,很像別的睡蓮葉。

passages.original: It was tied to a water-plant in the middle of the pond.
passages.vernacular: 佢繫喺池塘中央嘅一棵水草上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它繫在池塘中央的一棵水草上。

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy took a reed pole, and pushed the boat out into open water. "I know a good place for minnows," said Mr. Jeremy Fisher.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生攞咗一根蘆葦桿,把船推向開闊嘅水面。「我知道一個釣小魚嘅好地方,」傑里米·費舍先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生拿了一根蘆葦桿,把船推向開闊的水面。「我知道一個釣小魚的好地方,」傑里米·費舍先生說。

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy stuck his pole into the mud and fastened the boat to it.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生把桿子插進泥裡,把船拴喺上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生把桿子插進泥裡,把船拴在上面。

passages.original: Then he settled himself cross-legged and arranged his fishing tackle.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢盤腿坐好,整理佢嘅釣具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他盤腿坐好,整理他的釣具。

passages.original: He had the dearest little red float.
passages.vernacular: 佢有最可愛嘅小紅浮標。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有最可愛的小紅浮標。

passages.original: His rod was a tough stalk of grass, his line was a fine long white horse-hair, and he tied a little wriggling worm at the end.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅釣竿係一根結實嘅草莖,佢嘅釣線係一根又細又長嘅白馬毛,佢喺末端拴咗一條扭動嘅小蚯蚓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的釣竿是一根結實的草莖,他的釣線是一根又細又長的白馬毛,他在末端拴了一條扭動的小蚯蚓。

passages.original: The rain trickled down his back, and for nearly an hour he stared at the float.
passages.vernacular: 雨水順住佢嘅背流下嚟,佢盯住浮標睇咗將近一個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雨水順著他的背流下來,他盯著浮標看了將近一個小時。

passages.original: "This is getting tiresome, I think I should like some lunch," said Mr. Jeremy Fisher.
passages.vernacular: 「呢越嚟越乏味喇,我想我想食午飯喇,」傑里米·費舍先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這越來越乏味了,我想我想吃午飯了,」傑里米·費舍先生說。

passages.original: He punted back again amongst the water-plants, and took some lunch out of his basket.
passages.vernacular: 佢撐船回到水草中間,從籃子裡攞出午餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他撐船回到水草中間,從籃子裡拿出午餐。

passages.original: "I will eat a butterfly sandwich, and wait till the shower is over," said Mr. Jeremy Fisher.
passages.vernacular: 「我要食一個蝴蝶三明治,等陣雨過去,」傑里米·費舍先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要吃一個蝴蝶三明治,等陣雨過去,」傑里米·費舍先生說。

passages.original: A great big water-beetle came up underneath the lily leaf and tweaked the toe of one of his goloshes.
passages.vernacular: 一隻好大嘅水甲蟲從瞓蓮葉下面上嚟,扯咗扯佢一隻膠套鞋嘅鞋尖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻很大的水甲蟲從睡蓮葉下面上來,扯了扯他一隻膠套鞋的鞋尖。

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy crossed his legs up shorter, out of reach, and went on eating his sandwich.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生把腿盤得更緊,夠唔到嘅地方,繼續食佢嘅三明治。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生把腿盤得更緊,夠不到的地方,繼續吃他的三明治。

passages.original: Once or twice something moved about with a rustle and a splash amongst the rushes at the side of the pond.
passages.vernacular: 池塘邊嘅燈芯草叢中,有一兩次有嘢沙沙作響、濺起水花地走動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 池塘邊的燈芯草叢中,有一兩次有東西沙沙作響、濺起水花地走動。

passages.original: "I trust that is not a rat," said Mr. Jeremy Fisher; "I think I had better get away from here."
passages.vernacular: 「我希望嗰唔係老鼠,」傑里米·費舍先生講;「我想我最好離開呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望那不是老鼠,」傑里米·費舍先生說;「我想我最好離開這裡。」

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy shoved the boat out again a little way, and dropped in the bait.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生又把船推出去啲,放下魚餌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生又把船推出去一點,放下魚餌。

passages.original: There was a bite almost directly; the float gave a tremendous bobbit!
passages.vernacular: 幾乎即刻就有魚咬鉤;浮標猛地一沉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎立刻就有魚咬鉤;浮標猛地一沉!

passages.original: "A minnow! a minnow!
passages.vernacular: 「一條小魚!一條小魚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一條小魚!一條小魚!

passages.original: I have him by the nose!" cried Mr. Jeremy Fisher, jerking up his rod.
passages.vernacular: 我抓住佢嘅鼻子喇!」傑里米·費舍先生喊道,猛地提起釣竿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我抓住它的鼻子了!」傑里米·費舍先生喊道,猛地提起釣竿。

passages.original: But what a horrible surprise!
passages.vernacular: 不過幾咁可怕嘅驚訝啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是多麼可怕的驚訝啊!

passages.original: Instead of a smooth fat minnow, Mr. Jeremy landed little Jack Sharp the stickleback, covered with spines!
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生釣上嚟嘅唔係一條光滑肥胖嘅小魚,而係渾身係刺嘅小棘魚傑克·夏普!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生釣上來的不是一條光滑肥胖的小魚,而是渾身是刺的小棘魚傑克·夏普!

passages.original: The stickleback floundered about the boat, pricking and snapping until he was quite out of breath.
passages.vernacular: 棘魚喺船裡亂蹦,又扎又咬,直到佢上氣不接下氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 棘魚在船裡亂蹦,又扎又咬,直到他上氣不接下氣。

passages.original: Then he jumped back into the water.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢跳回水裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他跳回水裡。

passages.original: And a shoal of other little fishes put their heads out, and laughed at Mr. Jeremy Fisher.
passages.vernacular: 一大群別嘅小魚探出頭嚟,嘲笑傑里米·費舍先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一大群別的小魚探出頭來,嘲笑傑里米·費舍先生。

passages.original: And while Mr. Jeremy sat disconsolately on the edge of his boat--sucking his sore fingers and peering down into the water--a much worse thing happened; a really frightful thing it would have been, if Mr. Jeremy had not been wearing a macintosh!
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生沮喪地坐喺船邊——吮住佢疼痛嘅手指,向水裡窺睇時——發生咗更糟得多嘅事;如果傑里米先生冇穿雨衣,嗰將係一件真正可怕嘅事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生沮喪地坐在船邊——吮著他疼痛的手指,向水裡窺看時——發生了更糟得多的事;如果傑里米先生沒有穿雨衣,那將是一件真正可怕的事!

passages.original: A great big enormous trout came up--ker-pflop-p-p-p! with a splash--and it seized Mr. Jeremy with a snap, "Ow!
passages.vernacular: 一條又大又大嘅鱒魚浮上嚟——嘩啦啪——濺起水花——佢猛地一口咬住傑里米先生:「哎喲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條又大又大的鱒魚浮上來——嘩啦啪——濺起水花——它猛地一口咬住傑里米先生:「哎喲!

passages.original: Ow!
passages.vernacular: 哎喲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎喲!

passages.original: Ow!"--and then it turned and dived down to the bottom of the pond!
passages.vernacular: 哎喲!」——然後佢轉身潛到咗池塘底!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎喲!」——然後它轉身潛到了池塘底!

passages.original: But the trout was so displeased with the taste of the macintosh, that in less than half a minute it spat him out again; and the only thing it swallowed was Mr. Jeremy's goloshes.
passages.vernacular: 不過鱒魚對雨衣嘅味道咁不滿意,唔到半分鐘就把佢又吐咗出嚟;佢吞下去嘅只有傑里米先生嘅膠套鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是鱒魚對雨衣的味道那麼不滿意,不到半分鐘就把他又吐了出來;它吞下去的只有傑里米先生的膠套鞋。

passages.original: Mr. Jeremy bounced up to the surface of the water, like a cork and the bubbles out of a soda water bottle; and he swam with all his might to the edge of the pond.
passages.vernacular: 傑里米先生像軟木塞同汽水瓶裡嘅氣泡一樣彈到水面上;佢拚命游向池塘邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里米先生像軟木塞和汽水瓶裡的氣泡一樣彈到水面上;他拚命游向池塘邊。

passages.original: He scrambled out on the first bank he came to, and he hopped home across the meadow with his macintosh all in tatters.
passages.vernacular: 佢爬上遇到嘅第一個岸,穿過草地蹦蹦跳跳地回家,雨衣已破成碎片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他爬上遇到的第一個岸,穿過草地蹦蹦跳跳地回家,雨衣已破成碎片。

passages.original: "What a mercy that was not a pike!" said Mr. Jeremy Fisher. "I have lost my rod and basket; but it does not much matter, for I am sure I should never have dared to go fishing again!"
passages.vernacular: 「幸好嗰唔係梭子魚!」傑里米·費舍先生講。「我丟咗釣竿同籃子;不過冇乜嘢大關係,因為我肯定再都唔敢去釣魚喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幸好那不是梭子魚!」傑里米·費舍先生說。「我丟了釣竿和籃子;不過沒什麼大關係,因為我肯定再也不敢去釣魚了!」

passages.original: He put some sticking plaster on his fingers, and his friends both came to dinner.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺手指上貼咗啲膠布,佢嘅兩個朋友都嚟食飯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在手指上貼了一些膠布,他的兩個朋友都來吃飯了。

passages.original: He could not offer them fish, but he had something else in his larder.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠請佢哋食魚,不過佢嘅食品櫃裡仲有別嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不能請他們吃魚,可是他的食品櫃裡還有別的東西。

passages.original: Sir Isaac Newton wore his black and gold waistcoat,
passages.vernacular: 艾薩克·牛頓爵士穿住佢嘅黑金背心,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾薩克·牛頓爵士穿著他的黑金背心,

passages.original: And Mr. Alderman Ptolemy Tortoise brought a salad with him in a string bag.
passages.vernacular: 托勒密·烏龜市議員帶嚟咗一份沙拉,裝喺一個網兜裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托勒密·烏龜市議員帶來了一份沙拉,裝在一個網兜裡。

passages.original: And instead of a nice dish of minnows--they had a roasted grasshopper with lady-bird sauce; which frogs consider a beautiful treat; but I think it must have been nasty!
passages.vernacular: 而唔係一盤美味嘅小魚——佢哋食咗烤蚱蜢配瓢蟲醬;青蛙哋認為呢個係美味佳餚;不過我想佢一定好難食!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而不是一盤美味的小魚——他們吃了烤蚱蜢配瓢蟲醬;青蛙們認為這是美味佳餚;可是我想它一定很難吃!

chapters.title: The Tale of the Flopsy Bunnies 福洛西兔寶寶的故事

passages.original: CH It is said that the effect of eating too much lettuce is "soporific."
passages.vernacular: 據講食太多萵苣會有「催眠」作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說吃太多萵苣會有「催眠」作用。

passages.original: I have never felt sleepy after eating lettuces; but then I am not a rabbit.
passages.vernacular: 我食咗萵苣從冇覺得睏;但我唔係兔子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我吃了萵苣從沒覺得睏;但我不是兔子。

passages.original: They certainly had a very soporific effect upon the Flopsy Bunnies!
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對福洛西兔寶寶哋確實有好強嘅催眠作用!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們對福洛西兔寶寶們確實有很強的催眠作用!

passages.original: When Benjamin Bunny grew up, he married his Cousin Flopsy.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明兔長大後,娶咗佢嘅堂妹福洛西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明兔長大後,娶了他的堂妹福洛西。

passages.original: They had a large family, and they were very improvident and cheerful.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋有一大家子,又不愛操心又快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們有一大家子,又不愛操心又快樂。

passages.original: I do not remember the separate names of their children; they were generally called the "Flopsy Bunnies."
passages.vernacular: 我不記得佢哋細路哋各自嘅名字;佢哋通常被叫作「福洛西兔寶寶」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不記得他們孩子們各自的名字;他們通常被叫作「福洛西兔寶寶」。

passages.original: As there was not always quite enough to eat,--Benjamin used to borrow cabbages from Flopsy's brother, Peter Rabbit, who kept a nursery garden.
passages.vernacular: 因為並不總是夠食,——班傑明常向福洛西嘅哥哥彼得兔借捲心菜,彼得開咗一個苗圃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為並不總是夠吃,——班傑明常向福洛西的哥哥彼得兔借捲心菜,彼得開了一個苗圃。

passages.original: Sometimes Peter Rabbit had no cabbages to spare.
passages.vernacular: 有時彼得兔冇多餘嘅捲心菜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時彼得兔沒有多餘的捲心菜。

passages.original: When this happened, the Flopsy Bunnies went across the field to a rubbish heap, in the ditch outside Mr. McGregor's garden.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣,福洛西兔寶寶哋就穿過田野,到麥克格雷格先生園子外面溝裡嘅一堆垃圾上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時,福洛西兔寶寶們就穿過田野,到麥克格雷格先生園子外面溝裡的一堆垃圾上去。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor's rubbish heap was a mixture.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生嘅垃圾堆係個大雜燴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生的垃圾堆是個大雜燴。

passages.original: There were jam pots and paper bags, and mountains of chopped grass from the mowing machine (which always tasted oily), and some rotten vegetable marrows and an old boot or two.
passages.vernacular: 有果醬罐、紙袋,割草機割下嘅堆積如山嘅草(總是帶住油味),仲有啲爛咗嘅西葫蘆同一兩隻舊靴子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有果醬罐、紙袋,割草機割下的堆積如山的草(總是帶著油味),還有一些爛了的西葫蘆和一兩隻舊靴子。

passages.original: One day--oh joy!--there were a quantity of overgrown lettuces, which had "shot" into flower.
passages.vernacular: 有一天——哦,太高興喇!——有大量長老嘅萵苣,已經抽薹開花喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天——哦,太高興了!——有大量長老的萵苣,已經抽薹開花了。

passages.original: The Flopsy Bunnies simply stuffed lettuces.
passages.vernacular: 福洛西兔寶寶哋只管把萵苣往肚子裡塞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福洛西兔寶寶們只管把萵苣往肚子裡塞。

passages.original: By degrees, one after another, they were overcome with slumber, and lay down in the mown grass.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地,一個接一個,佢哋被瞓意征服,躺倒喺剛割嘅草裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地,一個接一個,他們被睡意征服,躺倒在剛割的草裡。

passages.original: Benjamin was not so much overcome as his children.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明冇像佢嘅細路哋嗰樣被征服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明沒有像他的孩子們那樣被征服。

passages.original: Before going to sleep he was sufficiently wide awake to put a paper bag over his head to keep off the flies.
passages.vernacular: 瞓住之前,佢仲足夠清醒,把一個紙袋套喺頭上,防蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 睡著之前,他還足夠清醒,把一個紙袋套在頭上,防蒼蠅。

passages.original: The little Flopsy Bunnies slept delightfully in the warm sun.
passages.vernacular: 小福洛西兔寶寶哋喺溫暖嘅陽光下瞓得好香。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小福洛西兔寶寶們在溫暖的陽光下睡得很香。

passages.original: From the lawn beyond the garden came the distant clacketty sound of the mowing machine.
passages.vernacular: 從花園外面嘅草坪上傳嚟割草機遠遠嘅咔噠咔噠聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從花園外面的草坪上傳來割草機遠遠的咔噠咔噠聲。

passages.original: The bluebottles buzzed about the wall, and a little old mouse picked over the rubbish among the jam pots.
passages.vernacular: 青蠅喺牆邊嗡嗡飛,一隻小老鼠喺果醬罐中間翻揀垃圾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 青蠅在牆邊嗡嗡飛,一隻小老鼠在果醬罐中間翻揀垃圾。

passages.original: (I can tell you her name, she was called Thomasina Tittlemouse, a woodmouse with a long tail.)
passages.vernacular: (我可以告訴你佢嘅名字,佢叫托馬西娜·蒂特爾茅斯,係一隻長尾巴嘅林鼠。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (我可以告訴你她的名字,她叫托馬西娜·蒂特爾茅斯,是一隻長尾巴的林鼠。)

passages.original: She rustled across the paper bag, and awakened Benjamin Bunny.
passages.vernacular: 佢沙沙地從紙袋上爬過,把班傑明兔吵醒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沙沙地從紙袋上爬過,把班傑明兔吵醒了。

passages.original: The mouse apologized profusely, and said that she knew Peter Rabbit.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠連聲道歉,講佢認識彼得兔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠連聲道歉,說她認識彼得兔。

passages.original: While she and Benjamin were talking, close under the wall, they heard a heavy tread above their heads; and suddenly Mr. McGregor emptied out a sackful of lawn mowings right upon the top of the sleeping Flopsy Bunnies!
passages.vernacular: 佢同班傑明喺牆下講話時,佢哋聽見頭頂上沉重嘅腳步聲;突然麥克格雷格先生把一整袋草坪嘅碎草正倒喺瞓住嘅福洛西兔寶寶哋身上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她和班傑明在牆下說話時,他們聽見頭頂上沉重的腳步聲;突然麥克格雷格先生把一整袋草坪的碎草正倒在睡著的福洛西兔寶寶們身上!

passages.original: Benjamin shrank down under his paper bag.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明縮到佢嘅紙袋底下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明縮到他的紙袋底下。

passages.original: The mouse hid in a jam pot.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠躲進一個果醬罐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠躲進一個果醬罐。

passages.original: The little rabbits smiled sweetly in their sleep under the shower of grass; they did not awake because the lettuces had been so soporific.
passages.vernacular: 小兔子哋喺草雨下甜甜地微笑住瞓;佢哋冇醒,因為萵苣嘅催眠作用咁強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小兔子們在草雨下甜甜地微笑著睡;他們沒有醒,因為萵苣的催眠作用那麼強。

passages.original: They dreamt that their mother Flopsy was tucking them up in a hay bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋夢見媽媽福洛西喺把佢哋塞進乾草床裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們夢見媽媽福洛西在把他們塞進乾草床裡。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor looked down after emptying his sack.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生倒空袋子後往下睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生倒空袋子後往下看。

passages.original: He saw some funny little brown tips of ears sticking up through the lawn mowings.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇見啲滑稽嘅小棕色耳朵尖從碎草中豎咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看見一些滑稽的小棕色耳朵尖從碎草中豎了出來。

passages.original: He stared at them for some time.
passages.vernacular: 佢盯住佢哋睇咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他盯著它們看了一會兒。

passages.original: Presently a fly settled on one of them and it moved.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒一隻蒼蠅落喺其中一個上面,佢動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒一隻蒼蠅落在其中一個上面,它動了。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor climbed down on to the rubbish heap--
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生爬下到垃圾堆上——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生爬下到垃圾堆上——

passages.original: "One, two, three, four! five! six leetle rabbits!" said he as he dropped them into his sack.
passages.vernacular: 「一、二、三、四!五!六隻小兔子!」佢一邊把佢哋放進袋子裡一邊講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一、二、三、四!五!六隻小兔子!」他一邊把它們放進袋子裡一邊說。

passages.original: The Flopsy Bunnies dreamt that their mother was turning them over in bed.
passages.vernacular: 福洛西兔寶寶哋夢見媽媽喺床上畀佢哋翻身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福洛西兔寶寶們夢見媽媽在床上給他們翻身。

passages.original: They stirred a little in their sleep, but still they did not wake up.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺瞓夢中微微動咗動,可定係冇醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在睡夢中微微動了動,可還是沒醒。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor tied up the sack and left it on the wall.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生紮緊袋子,把佢放喺牆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生紮緊袋子,把它放在牆上。

passages.original: He went to put away the mowing machine.
passages.vernacular: 佢去收起割草機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他去收起割草機。

passages.original: While he was gone, Mrs. Flopsy Bunny (who had remained at home) came across the field.
passages.vernacular: 佢不喺嘅時候,福洛西兔太太(一直待喺家裡嘅)穿過田野過嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不在的時候,福洛西兔太太(一直待在家裡的)穿過田野過來了。

passages.original: She looked suspiciously at the sack and wondered where everybody was?
passages.vernacular: 佢懷疑地睇住嗰個袋子,納悶大家都喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她懷疑地看著那個袋子,納悶大家都在哪裡?

passages.original: Then the mouse came out of her jam pot, and Benjamin took the paper bag off his head, and they told the doleful tale.
passages.vernacular: 然後老鼠從佢嘅果醬罐裡出嚟,班傑明把紙袋從頭上摘下嚟,佢哋講述咗呢悲傷嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後老鼠從她的果醬罐裡出來,班傑明把紙袋從頭上摘下來,他們講述了這悲傷的故事。

passages.original: Benjamin and Flopsy were in despair, they could not undo the string.
passages.vernacular: 班傑明同福洛西絕望喇,佢哋解不開繩子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班傑明和福洛西絕望了,他們解不開繩子。

passages.original: But Mrs. Tittlemouse was a resourceful person.
passages.vernacular: 但蒂特爾茅斯太太係個足智多謀嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但蒂特爾茅斯太太是個足智多謀的人。

passages.original: She nibbled a hole in the bottom corner of the sack.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺袋子底部嘅一角啃咗個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在袋子底部的一角啃了個洞。

passages.original: The little rabbits were pulled out and pinched to wake them.
passages.vernacular: 小兔子哋被拉咗出嚟,又被捏咗一下弄醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小兔子們被拉了出來,又被捏了一下弄醒。

passages.original: Their parents stuffed the empty sack with three rotten vegetable marrows, an old blacking-brush and two decayed turnips.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅父母把空袋子裡塞進三個爛西葫蘆、一把舊嘅擦鞋刷同兩個爛蕪菁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的父母把空袋子裡塞進三個爛西葫蘆、一把舊的擦鞋刷和兩個爛蕪菁。

passages.original: Then they all hid under a bush and watched for Mr. McGregor.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋都躲喺一叢灌木下,睇住麥克格雷格先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們都躲在一叢灌木下,看著麥克格雷格先生。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor came back and picked up the sack, and carried it off.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生回嚟,拎起袋子,攞走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生回來,拎起袋子,拿走了。

passages.original: He carried it hanging down, as if it were rather heavy.
passages.vernacular: 佢拎住佢往下垂,好像佢相當重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拎著它往下垂,好像它相當重。

passages.original: The Flopsy Bunnies followed at a safe distance.
passages.vernacular: 福洛西兔寶寶哋喺安全距離外跟住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 福洛西兔寶寶們在安全距離外跟著。

passages.original: They watched him go into his house.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇住佢走進佢嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看著他走進他的房子。

passages.original: And then they crept up to the window to listen.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋爬到窗前偷聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們爬到窗前偷聽。

passages.original: Mr. McGregor threw down the sack on the stone floor in a way that would have been extremely painful to the Flopsy Bunnies, if they had happened to have been inside it.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生把袋子扔喺石頭地板上,如果福洛西兔寶寶哋碰巧喺裡面,嗰會好疼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生把袋子扔在石頭地板上,如果福洛西兔寶寶們碰巧在裡面,那會非常疼。

passages.original: They could hear him drag his chair on the flags, and chuckle--
passages.vernacular: 佢哋聽見佢喺石板上拖椅子,咯咯笑——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們聽見他在石板上拖椅子,咯咯笑——

passages.original: "One, two, three, four, five, six leetle rabbits!" said Mr. McGregor.
passages.vernacular: 「一、二、三、四、五、六隻小兔子!」麥克格雷格先生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一、二、三、四、五、六隻小兔子!」麥克格雷格先生說。

passages.original: "Eh?
What's that?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼?

passages.original: What have they been spoiling now?" enquired Mrs. McGregor.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又喺糟蹋乜嘢喇?」麥克格雷格太太問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又在糟蹋什麼了?」麥克格雷格太太問。

passages.original: "One, two, three, four, five, six leetle fat rabbits!" repeated Mr. McGregor, counting on his fingers--"one, two, three--"
passages.vernacular: 「一、二、三、四、五、六隻肥小兔子!」麥克格雷格先生重複,掰著手指數——「一、二、三——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一、二、三、四、五、六隻肥小兔子!」麥克格雷格先生重複,掰著手指數——「一、二、三——」

passages.original: "Don't you be silly; what do you mean, you silly old man?"
passages.vernacular: 「別傻喇;你乜嘢意思,你呢個傻老頭?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別傻了;你什麼意思,你這個傻老頭?」

passages.original: "In the sack! one, two, three, four, five, six!" replied Mr. McGregor.
passages.vernacular: 「喺袋子裡!一、二、三、四、五、六!」麥克格雷格先生回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在袋子裡!一、二、三、四、五、六!」麥克格雷格先生回答。

passages.original: (The youngest Flopsy Bunny got upon the window-sill.)
passages.vernacular: (最小嘅福洛西兔寶寶爬上咗窗台。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (最小的福洛西兔寶寶爬上了窗台。)

passages.original: Mrs. McGregor took hold of the sack and felt it.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格太太抓住袋子摸咗摸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格太太抓住袋子摸了摸。

passages.original: She said she could feel six, but they must be old rabbits, because they were so hard and all different shapes.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢能摸到六個,但佢哋一定係老兔子,因為佢哋咁硬,形狀各異。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她能摸到六個,但它們一定是老兔子,因為它們那麼硬,形狀各異。

passages.original: "Not fit to eat; but the skins will do fine to line my old cloak."
passages.vernacular: 「唔能夠食;不過皮用嚟襯我嘅舊斗篷正合適。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不能吃;不過皮用來襯我的舊斗篷正合適。」

passages.original: "Line your old cloak?" shouted Mr. McGregor--"I shall sell them and buy myself baccy!"
passages.vernacular: 「襯你嘅舊斗篷?」麥克格雷格先生喊道——「我要把佢哋賣喇,畀自己買煙草!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「襯你的舊斗篷?」麥克格雷格先生喊道——「我要把它們賣了,給自己買煙草!」

passages.original: "Rabbit tobacco!
passages.vernacular: 「兔子煙草!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兔子煙草!

passages.original: I shall skin them and cut off their heads."
passages.vernacular: 我要把佢哋剝皮,砍掉腦袋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把它們剝皮,砍掉腦袋。」

passages.original: Mrs. McGregor untied the sack and put her hand inside.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格太太解開袋子,把手伸咗進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格太太解開袋子,把手伸了進去。

passages.original: When she felt the vegetables she became very very angry.
passages.vernacular: 佢摸到蔬菜時,變得好好生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她摸到蔬菜時,變得非常非常生氣。

passages.original: She said that Mr. McGregor had "done it a purpose."
passages.vernacular: 佢講麥克格雷格先生係「故意嘅」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說麥克格雷格先生是「故意的」。

passages.original: And Mr. McGregor was very angry too.
passages.vernacular: 麥克格雷格先生都好生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麥克格雷格先生也非常生氣。

passages.original: One of the rotten marrows came flying through the kitchen window, and hit the youngest Flopsy Bunny.
passages.vernacular: 一隻爛西葫蘆從廚房窗子飛出嚟,砸喺最小嘅福洛西兔寶寶身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻爛西葫蘆從廚房窗子飛出來,砸在最小的福洛西兔寶寶身上。

passages.original: It was rather hurt.
passages.vernacular: 佢相當疼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它相當疼。

passages.original: Then Benjamin and Flopsy thought that it was time to go home.
passages.vernacular: 於是班傑明同福洛西想,係回家嘅時候喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是班傑明和福洛西想,是回家的時候了。

passages.original: So Mr. McGregor did not get his tobacco, and Mrs. McGregor did not get her rabbit skins.
passages.vernacular: 所以麥克格雷格先生冇攞到佢嘅煙草,麥克格雷格太太都冇攞到佢嘅兔皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以麥克格雷格先生沒有拿到他的煙草,麥克格雷格太太也沒有拿到她的兔皮。

passages.original: But next Christmas Thomasina Tittlemouse got a present of enough rabbit-wool to make herself a cloak and a hood, and a handsome muff and a pair of warm mittens.
passages.vernacular: 但係下個聖誕節,托馬西娜·蒂特爾茅斯得到一份禮物,係足夠畀佢做一件斗篷同風帽,仲有一個漂亮嘅暖手筒同一副暖同嘅手套嘅兔毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是下個聖誕節,托馬西娜·蒂特爾茅斯得到一份禮物,是足夠給她做一件斗篷和風帽,還有一個漂亮的暖手筒和一副暖和的手套的兔毛。
